Passengers and cab drivers at Bengaluru's Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) have accused ride-hailing platforms of manipulating cab availability to push up fares, even as hundreds of taxis allegedly remain idle in airport parking areas, according to a report by Deccan Herald. The reported complaints come amid long passenger queues, failed bookings and extended waiting periods for drivers. Commuters have alleged that they are being pushed towards more expensive cab categories when their preferred rides are unavailable, while drivers say they often spend hours waiting for a single booking, as per the report. The situation has also been compounded by a reported decline in passenger traffic, particularly at the international terminal, which drivers have partly attributed to tensions in West Asia and disruptions to air travel. G Narayana Swamy, president of Karnataka Chalakara Okkuta, told Deccan Herald that hundreds of cabs could be seen parked in the airport's P7 parking zone even as passengers faced long queues at pickup points. He alleged that some authorised cab operators were deliberately restricting vehicle availability to drive up fares. Bangalore International Airport Limited (BIAL), which operates the airport, has nine authorised cab partners, including KSTDC, Mega Cabs, Uber, Uber Black, Ola, Quick Ride, OHM Electric Cabs and WTI, as per the report. Passengers have reported waiting between 40 and 60 minutes to secure a ride. Some said their initial bookings did not materialise, leaving them with the option of booking more expensive vehicle categories. A passenger travelling from Goa told Deccan Herald that she found at least 60 people waiting at the Uber kiosk when she arrived at around 7 PM last week. Quick Ride had only one pre-booked SUV available, while drivers at the Namma Yatri kiosk reportedly said that only SUVs could be arranged. The passenger said that after waiting for around 45 minutes, the driver assigned to her booking refused the trip because her destination was not close enough to the airport. She was travelling to Marathahalli. She also alleged that another driver demanded an additional fare, raising concerns over the availability of airport taxis and the enforcement of fare rules. Cab drivers have also raised concerns about declining passenger traffic and operational restrictions, saying these are affecting their earnings. According to the report, drivers said they sometimes wait between two and three hours for a single booking. They are required to remain in designated parking areas until their ride-hailing applications clear them to enter the passenger pickup zone. Drivers have particularly flagged weaker demand at the international terminal, which they partly attribute to tensions in West Asia and disruptions to flight operations. A premium cab operator at the airport said it deploys around 800 vehicles across both terminals, with the bulk of demand concentrated at Terminal 1. The operator told the daily that services generally run smoothly outside peak hours, but longer trip durations affect vehicle availability. He closely follows diplomatic developments in New Delhi and has a keen interest in defence and national security.

Bhanu also focuses on in-depth, interview-based reports and regularly speaking with experts and policymakers to bring perspectives and context to major developments around the world.

He is also interested in stories with strong humanitarian angles.

One such report examined the cases of Indian nationals who were allegedly recruited and forced into Russia’s war against Ukraine. While reporting the story, Bhanu spoke to the families of those affected and documented their experiences. The report was later taken into account by the United Nations in its findings on human rights violations linked to the war in Ukraine.

For Bhanu, the zeal to produce meaningful and impactful journalism remains at the heart of his work.

He has previously worked with Firstpost, NDTV, Newslaundry and Republic.

Bhanu studied at the Delhi School of Journalism, University of Delhi. He initially chose science with plans to pursue engineering, influenced by conventional expectations, but fate had other plans and eventually led him to journalism.

Beyond the newsroom, Bhanu enjoys exploring culture and history and often spends his days off on heritage walks. He is also passionate about travelling, biking and listening to folk music.

Wayanad set to become India's first e-waste-free district on November 27
Wayanad in Keralam will be formally declared India's first completely e-waste-free district on November 27. The milestone highlights community-led waste management and advances wider plastic-free and carbon-neutral goals.
Wayanad is set to become India’s first completely e-waste-free district, Agriculture Minister T Siddique said on Tuesday, according to news agency PTI.
Chief Minister VD Satheesan is scheduled to make the formal declaration on November 27. The district will then launch a campaign to become plastic-free and environment-friendly, with carbon neutrality as its next target.
Siddique said the declaration would be made at a function at Chandragiri Auditorium in Kalpetta in the presence of Local Self-Government Minister KM Shaji, elected representatives and officials.
The achievement followed three months of coordinated efforts to collect electronic waste from households, government offices, educational institutions, tourist destinations and public establishments and send it for safe disposal, Siddique told PTI.
He credited local bodies, Haritha Karma Sena members, sanitation workers, government departments, officials, residents, traders and restaurant owners for helping the district achieve the target.
Siddique described the initiative as an important environmental conservation effort. He said hazardous chemicals from improperly discarded electronic waste could contaminate soil and water and pose serious risks to human health, agriculture and the ecosystem.
The campaign was not limited to removing waste but also aimed to protect Wayanad’s hills, forests, water resources and biodiversity for future generations, he said.
Siddique said the achievement would strengthen the state government’s ‘Nirmalam’ waste-free Kerala campaign, launched on Gandhi Jayanti. It would also show how public participation could support government initiatives in meeting major environmental goals, he added.
The state government aims to develop the hill district as a waste-free, environment-friendly and climate-resilient model by combining conservation of natural resources with sustainable development. Siddique said the initiative could inspire other districts across the country.
With the e-waste-free declaration scheduled for November 27, Wayanad will now focus on becoming plastic-free, environment-friendly and carbon-neutral.

49ers win in Mexico and Bills stay top - NFL week 11
- Published
The San Francisco 49ers and Buffalo Bills remain the pacesetters in each conference of the NFL after both won again.
The 49ers beat the Minnesota Vikings in the last of a record nine international games this season to take their record to 9-1.
They lead the way in the NFC, with the Chicago Bears and their divisional rivals the Detroit Lions next best on 8-2.
Buffalo improved to 9-1 for the first time since 1991 and lead the AFC from another pair of divisional rivals, with the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos on 8-2.
The Chiefs and Broncos could be joined by the Cincinnati Bengals, who conclude week 11 at the Washington Commanders on Monday.
49ers outsmart Vikings defence
Mexico hosted the first regular-season game to be played outside the US in October 2005, and the NFL returned to the country on Sunday following a four-year absence.
After being redeveloped for the 2026 World Cup, the Azteca Stadium staged its sixth NFL game and the third involving San Francisco, who kicked off this season's international series by beating the Los Angeles Rams in Australia in week one.
Sunday's game pitted the league's best offence against the best defence and was the first international game to be played in the primetime slot.
The Vikings defence had not conceded more than 23 points in a game this season, but the 49ers offence outsmarted them in front of 85,612 fans in Mexico City.
The 49ers scored four touchdowns in the first half - two by George Kittle - before running out 35-10 winners.
Mike Evans returned after missing three games with an Achilles problem to finish with 109 receiving yards and a touchdown.
With the game played at high altitude - about 7,220ft (2,240m) above sea level - some players used oxygen masks on the sidelines.
San Francisco face another test of their Super Bowl credentials next Sunday at home to the defending champions, the 6-4 Seattle Seahawks, who were one of six teams on their bye this week.
Giants secure statement win
The Jacksonville Jaguars entered week 11 with the best regular-season record over the past 12 months - they had lost only twice - and had scored more than 30 points in each of their past four games.
Yet the New York Giants managed to stifle the Jaguars for three quarters and led 20-6 heading into what proved to be a dramatic final quarter.
The Jaguars had to settle for a field goal after a controversial call denied them a touchdown, but they still threatened a fightback as they cut the deficit to five.
The Giants offence did enough to stop the Jags getting one more possession, though, and secure a 23-18 home win.
It was the first time the NFC East leaders have beaten a team with a winning record this season and they are now 6-3-1, while the 7-3 Jags remain in charge of the AFC South.
In his first season as head coach, John Harbaugh could lead the Giants to their first division title since 2011, when 'Big Blue' went on to claim their fourth Super Bowl.
They remain clear of the 5-6 Dallas Cowboys, whose rollercoaster season continued with a 51-30 win over the Tennessee Titans, with Dak Prescott throwing for 325 yards and four touchdowns.
Kelce at the double before tough Chiefs run
Although Josh Allen threw for more interceptions than touchdowns (2-1), the Bills were still comfortable, beating the Miami Dolphins 26-9 for their sixth straight victory.
The Bills have a mouth-watering Thanksgiving clash on Thursday (01:20 GMT, Friday) at home to the Kansas City Chiefs, who beat the Arizona Cardinals 34-7.
Travis Kelce had two scores for the Chiefs, claiming multiple touchdowns in the same game for the first time since a play-off win over Buffalo in January 2024.
Emmett Johnson registered a combined 143 yards and a touchdown in the absence of fellow running back Kenneth Walker, who is set to return from a minor groin problem against Buffalo.
That game kicks off a crucial five-game stretch for Kansas City, which continues against the Rams, the Bengals, the Patriots and the 49ers.
The Chiefs are joint top of the AFC West with the Denver Broncos, who kept the pressure on by beating the Las Vegas Raiders 38-24 for a sixth straight win.
Fernando Mendoza, this year's first overall draft pick, threw his first three touchdown passes but then a pick-six which allowed Denver to clinch victory, after Jonah Coleman had run in three scores for the Broncos.
Bears and Lions set up Thanksgiving showdown
The home team won all seven of the early games, and they were favourites heading into all but one of those match-ups.
The only underdogs to emerge victorious were the Philadelphia Eagles (3-7), who beat the Pittsburgh Steelers 19-16 to end a seven-game losing streak.
The Bears and Lions both won to remain joint-top of the NFC North, and they have a Thanksgiving showdown in Detroit on Thursday (18:00 GMT).
The Bears beat the New Orleans Saints 21-13, with Chicago's Jeffery Simmons claiming three sacks, taking his tally to five in three games since his blockbuster trade from Tennessee.
On Thursday he will try to stop this season's rushing leader Jahmyr Gibbs, who rushed for another 98 yards and two touchdowns in Detroit's 31-21 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
The NFL's highest-paid running back has now tied Barry Sanders for the most rushing touchdowns (52) before turning 25 – and Gibbs' birthday is not until March.

As far as trailblazers go, Kadambini Ganguly will figure right on top of several lists. She was a pioneering woman physician, the first to practise successfully in India, a gynaecologist and a social reformer who, equally efficiently, managed a large family as well. The story of Kadambini Ganguly is one of extraordinary achievement, and if told widely, will continue to inspire the young women of today.
In a profile published in Cureus in 2024, the authors point to the influence of the progressive Bramho Samaj movement, initiated by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, that helped Kadambini emerge from the shackles of conservative orthodoxy that might have stiffled her immense talent. “This environment, which championed the values of education and gender equality, contributed significantly to shaping her exemplary career and lifelong dedication to social justice,” the article reads. Records of her life acknowledge that she was partly recognised during her lifetime, but also mercilessly criticised and defamed for being a progressive, working woman. The full recognition of her contributions in medicine and the social sector came much later, only in recent decades.

The story so far: India continues to account for nearly a quarter of the world’s tuberculosis (TB) burden despite expanded diagnosis and treatment services, falling short of the national target of eliminating TB by 2025. According to the World Health Organization’s (WHO) Global Tuberculosis Report, released on November 12, 2026, an estimated 10.6 million people developed TB worldwide in 2025.
While India’s estimated TB mortality rate fell by 38%, from 28 deaths per lakh population in 2015 to 18 per lakh in 2025, the country diagnosed and notified 25.3 lakh cases during the year. However, the WHO has not published India’s estimated incidence for that year, as the figures are under review.

Malaysia to repatriate another 6,803 Myanmar nationals despite ICJ genocide ruling
Malaysia's Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim says the country plans to repatriate another 6,803 Myanmar nationals next month
KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia -- Malaysia will repatriate another 6,803 Myanmar nationals next month, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Tuesday as he defended the government's engagement with Myanmar's military leadership, despite a landmark international court ruling finding the country responsible for genocide against Rohingya Muslims.
The International Court of Justice, based in The Hague, Netherlands, last week found Myanmar guilty of genocide against its Rohingya minority, with evidence showing Myanmar forces killed about 10,000 Rohingya in a 2017 military operation that included mass rapes and killings, and the destruction of thousands of homes.
Myanmar’s government has dismissed the ruling as unfair. Anwar told Parliament that Malaysia respected the ICJ's ruling, but would continue to engage Myanmar's leadership to facilitate the repatriation of refugees.
Malaysia hosts nearly 200,000 refugees from Myanmar, including Rohingya who fled a military crackdown and members of other ethnic minorities. Anwar said that efforts to resettle them in third countries had been unsuccessful and Malaysia couldn't continue bearing the burden indefinitely.
He said that talks with Myanmar leader Min Aung Hlaing, who visited Kuala Lumpur last month, had helped bring progress to the long-standing issue.
Another 1,500 people will be sent back on three Myanmar naval vessels on Dec. 6 and 7, while another 5,303 will return throughout next month by air, with all costs borne by Myanmar, Anwar said.
A total of 10,476 Myanmar nationals have already been repatriated this year, including 1,476 who were taken home aboard a Myanmar naval vessel on Sept. 29, he said.
Malaysia had secured a guarantee of a “safe and dignified return” for those repatriated, Anwar said.
“So far, based on monitoring by Malaysian intelligence, none of the 10,476 individuals have been subjected to any form of pressure,” he said.
Despite the engagement with Myanmar, Anwar said that Malaysia remained committed to the Association of Southeast Asian Nations' peace plan on ending violence and resolving a prolonged crisis in Myanmar after the military seized power from the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi in 2021. It had sparked widespread opposition that plunged large parts of the country into conflict.
The 11-nation regional bloc has renewed diplomatic pressure on Myanmar for failing to implement its peace initiative and restricted the country’s top leaders from major regional summits. Myanmar has slammed ASEAN for unfair treatment.

The National Medical Commission (NMC) has asked all government medical colleges and their attached hospitals across the country to onboard the Prime Minister’s Road Accident Victims’ Hospitalisation and Assured Treatment (PM-RAHAT) scheme to expand access to cashless emergency treatment for road accident victims.
In a communication to deans, directors and principals of government medical colleges and medical superintendents of attached hospitals, the NMC said the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare had requested its intervention to facilitate their participation in the scheme. The request followed a September 24 meeting of the steering committee monitoring its implementation, chaired by the Secretary of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, which emphasised wider engagement with the medical community.
The NMC has asked institutions to accord priority to onboarding, with the National Health Authority (NHA) guidelines providing the framework for empanelment and registration of hospitals.
Launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on February 13, 2026, PM-RAHAT provides cashless treatment of up to ₹1.5 lakh per road accident victim for a maximum of seven days from the date of the accident at designated hospitals. Non-designated hospitals can provide stabilisation treatment to ensure that emergency care is not delayed during the critical ‘golden hour’.
Under NHA guidelines, hospitals already empanelled under the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) will be deemed eligible. Other facilities can be empanelled under the ‘PM-RAHAT Only’ category, while hospitals capable of providing initial stabilisation can register under ‘PM-RAHAT Lite’.
Designated hospitals must have round-the-clock emergency services, intensive care units, operation theatres, imaging and blood storage facilities, and specialists in trauma care, emergency medicine, general surgery and orthopaedics.
The guidelines also prioritise hospitals near identified accident hotspots, National and State Highways and other accident-prone road networks. State Road Safety Councils will coordinate implementation, while the NHA will maintain the digital platforms for hospital onboarding and claims management.

The Trump administration recently admitted in federal court that it deported a US citizen to Mexico after American authorities incorrectly concluded he was an undocumented immigrant.
Attorneys for the US justice department made that admission on Friday while requesting the dismissal of a lawsuit for damages that the deported man – Brian José Morales García of Austin, Texas – has been pursuing against the federal government.
Morales García’s case took that turn as the White House has faced bipartisan criticism for the aggressive mass deportation campaign pursued by Donald Trump throughout his second presidency – widely seen as a factor in the electoral battering his Republican party suffered during the 3 November midterms, costing it control of Congress.
The Denver-born, Mexico-raised Morales García was riding with his boss to his job as an air-conditioning installation technician on 3 April when they were pulled over by state and local officers near Fredericksburg, Texas.
Morales García was his boss’s passenger and did not have his identification on him. The 25-year-old also told the officers that he had his birth certificate and social security card at home, but they didn’t believe him – so they called immigration agents, who detained Morales García.
Court filings recount how Robert Gil Jr, a US Customs and Border Protection agent, consulted records from Mexico that listed a Mexican birthplace for Morales García. Gil Jr also accused Morales García of saying he was born in Mexico and observed that he only spoke in Spanish, according to court records.
Morales García was deported on 7 April, with the Trump administration later accusing him in a media statement of being in the country illegally.
Morales García’s attorneys sued on 1 May, maintaining that he had falsely said he entered the US illegally and signed papers for a rapid deportation in response to threats of imprisonment by agents. His lawsuit, which seeks an unspecified amount of money, also contended that family and friends tried to deliver documents proving his US citizenship before this deportation.
But those efforts were unduly rebuffed, Morales García’s lawsuit said.
The Trump administration denied Morales García’s assertions, saying on Friday that he went to Mexico voluntarily and therefore lacked any basis to sue the federal government for damages. Nonetheless, in court filings on Friday, the administration conceded that Morales García “was permitted entry” back into the US on 30 August after it reviewed “information concerning plaintiff’s place of birth”.
“Plaintiff is a dual citizen of the United States and Mexico,” Justin Simmons, the US attorney for the western district of Texas, wrote in a court filing first reported by the Texas Tribune.
Americans are not required to carry proof of citizenship when going about their daily business. Lawyers across the US have seen cases such as Morales García’s, which begin after an encounter with local authorities demonstrate how those officials are generally not aware of the nuances of immigration policy.
Texas’s public safety department is among many US state and local agencies that collaborate with federal immigration authorities under their 287(g) program.
The judge presiding over Morales García’s lawsuit, Robert Lee Pitman, did not immediately rule on the Trump administration’s request on Friday to dismiss the case. The lawsuit also named unspecified local and state Texas law enforcement officers as defendants.
An October 2025 report by ProPublica found that immigration agents had detained more than 170 US citizens during the first nine months of Trump’s second presidency.
Meanwhile, the media statement incorrectly saying Morales García was in the US illegally is among several related to immigration enforcement under the Trump administration that has unraveled under scrutiny.
A Guardian analysis published in July reviewed Trump administration press releases on 26 cases of cars allegedly being used to assault immigration enforcement agents – and nearly all were either disproven or dropped.

A cancer medicine supplied to a retailer for ₹2,700 carries a maximum retail price (MRP) of ₹27,000. Who accounts for this tenfold difference? This was among the examples highlighted by the Supreme Court in September 2026, when it questioned the gap between the prices paid for medicines and what patients ultimately pay.
Subsequently, on October 17, the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) announced a 30% cap on trade margins for 137 anti-cancer drugs, effective from November 9. This intervention could reduce prices substantially for some products. It also raises a broader question: how does India decide what medicines should cost?

After Nvidia’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Appearing on Stephen A. Smith’s radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would “end up on his feet.”
Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang
Trump got his wish to reinstate Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia — but investigations are still looming.
Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang
Trump got his wish to reinstate Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia — but investigations are still looming.
“You know the expression, anybody can be replaced,” Trump said, floating Apple’s ex-CEO Tim Cook as a potential CEO candidate.
It didn’t take long for Trump to begin softening his approach, making it clear he’d welcome Huang back into the role of CEO even if Nvidia’s own board wasn’t ready to do so. Behind the scenes, the Trump administration was working to grease the landing for Huang’s return. And soon, Nvidia’s board changed its tune: Barely a week after insisting they all agreed to shut the door on Huang’s return, they voted unanimously to reinstate him as CEO, president, and board director.
“There’s nothing wrong with a comeback,” Trump said in a celebratory call to CNBC.
Trump then posted an image on Truth Social of Huang transposed onto Trump’s own body in the infamous photo of him raising his fist after being shot at a campaign rally. In his raised fist, Huang-on-Trump’s-body is clutching a scarlet bra, holding it high in the air.
“There’s nothing wrong with a comeback”
Even after a decisive blow to the president’s power as Democrats swept the midterm elections, Trump appears to maintain his position as a corporate kingmaker. Trump said he spoke with Huang the night prior to his reinstatement and had been in communication with the board both “directly and indirectly.” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement that “President Trump was totally involved” in the board’s decision — Trump decided near the end of last week that he wanted to lead efforts to get Huang reappointed, per The New York Times, so he asked Vice President JD Vance to act as a liaison between Huang and Nvidia’s board, providing reassurances that the move wouldn’t pose a security risk. Trump also reportedly dialed into Nvidia’s Sunday night board meeting to make the case for his return. “I made the deal,” he told CNBC on Monday.
News of Huang’s reappointment, nearly as dramatic as Sam Altman’s return to his CEO role after being voted out by OpenAI’s board in 2023, was a widespread shock to experts, analysts, and investors, particularly after Nvidia’s board had assured stakeholders on its quarterly earnings call last Tuesday that the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On Monday morning, a surge in NASDAQ-100 futures hit a circuit-breaker limit and caused a halt in trading over the volatility.
Trump has meddled in other messy incidents, including by repeatedly — and perhaps illegally — extending the deadline for TikTok to complete its sale to a US entity, and, he admitted on Monday, protecting Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Although he said on CNBC that Musk is “80 percent super genius, 20 percent he has other problems,” Trump said it’s important to protect people like him and Huang. “We have to protect our brilliant people because we don’t have enough.”
But the upcoming Democratic-majority Congress could test both Huang and Trump’s influence. As Republicans prepare for an open presidential primary in 2028, at least one potential candidate appears to be breaking with the president in their skepticism of Huang and Nvidia. And Democrats seem eager to probe both Nvidia and the Trump administration.
The past couple of weeks have been tumultuous for Nvidia. Huang admitted he had had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom some US intelligence officers reportedly believed to be a potential Chinese spy. There were nearly immediate reports of an additional affair with a direct report, as well as an alleged third affair with a second employee. Megaspeed has reportedly also been investigated for a broader attempt to illegally funnel advanced Nvidia chips to China. Huang himself has pushed to open up more chip sales to China, and he reportedly lied to the Nvidia board about his infidelity. He’s scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1st.
The Nvidia board tried to address concerns about Huang in its announcement Monday, writing that members “received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” It made assurances that the independent investigation it had kicked off about Huang and foreign intelligence would “proceed to conclusion” with Huang’s cooperation.
The board also said it had recently formed an entirely new National Security and Export Control Committee “comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks,” which is working with legal counsel and advisers who have national security experience. Nvidia will be hiring for a new C-suite position, the board said: chief compliance officer. The executive will “oversee compliance” across the company and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance committees. “NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries,” the board added.
Still, the reaction to Huang’s return reflects how small the chance of Huang’s return seemed before Trump’s efforts. Although Trump had previously cast doubt on multiple reports that Alice Huang was a spy, The New York Times reported on Sunday that she “kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year.” According to the Times, which cited multiple people with knowledge of US intelligence reports, Kang Wei — Alice Huang’s business partner and, by some reports, husband, who reportedly introduced her to the Nvidia CEO — worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency. But on Sunday evening, Trump still argued for Huang’s return and managed to continue flipping Nvidia’s board in his favor after a weekend’s worth of efforts.
“[I]ndefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible”
If the board maintained any hang-ups about bringing Huang back as CEO, Trump’s power over the executive branch — and the pressure he could exert with it — might have offered a compelling counterargument. The Securities and Exchange Commission had previously opened an investigation into whether Nvidia “misled investors,” according to The Wall Street Journal. But in a post on Truth Social Monday, Trump said that the attorney general “has confirmed that the U.S. Government does not possess evidence that he has engaged in any unlawful conduct.” Reached for comment, the DOJ did not provide an on-the-record response in line with The Verge’s editorial policy.
Key Democrats have indicated that both Nvidia and the Trump administration will be under fire when the new Congress is sworn in — and momentum has built behind GPU export controls, which Huang lobbied extensively to loosen. “Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain.” Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) said in a post on X, adding they’d work “on a bipartisan basis to continue advancing policies that stop the flow of our most powerful technology to the Chinese military and other adversaries.” Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) called the board’s decision “indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible” and pledged to investigate “business malfeasance by NVIDIA and corrupt abuse of power by Howard Lutnick and the Department of Commerce.” He called for “traditional Republicans” to join in the effort.
“The reckless decision to bring Jensen Huang back as CEO does not change the fact that Mr. Huang, NVIDIA executives, and the company’s board still owe Congress answers about the company’s compliance with U.S. export controls,” Sen. Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, said in a statement. “Jensen Huang’s return only increases the urgency of passing bipartisan export control bills into law and making sure NVIDIA does not lobby to kill that legislation and put our national security at risk.” Rep. Jamie Raskin, the top Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, said, “A real Congress will find out” whether Trump and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick had any alternative incentives for their role in Nvidia’s dealings. Sen. Mark Warner, the top Democrat on the Intelligence Committee, called Trump’s intervention to bring back Huang “outrageous.” Rep. Joaquin Castro (D-TX), a member of the House Intelligence and Foreign Affairs Committees, which are interviewing Huang next week, said he wants to know how Trump stands to benefit from “personally champion[ing] Huang’s return.”
“We need to know why Trump put his thumb on the scale to have Jensen reinstated as CEO”
At closed-door hearings next week, Democrats say they intend to press Huang and the administration further, and several accused the administration of corruption. “We need to know why Trump put his thumb on the scale to have Jensen reinstated as CEO and why his administration failed to restrict the PRC’s access to our most sensitive technology,” Rep. Gregory Meeks, the top Democrat on the House Foreign Affairs Committee, said in a statement to The Verge. The board’s decision is “outrageous,” said Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), a member of the House Select Committee on China. “We still don’t know what information Chinese intelligence may have obtained from him, and neither the government nor Nvidia’s own board has completed its investigation,” Krishnamoorthi said in a statement, calling for Huang to testify publicly. “Reinstatement is no substitute for accountability,” Rep. Kathy Castor (D-FL), another China Committee member, said in a statement.
California Attorney General Rob Bonta also intends to continue an investigation into the company. “The reinstatement of Jensen Huang does not change the fact that the American people deserve to know what happened here — whether Nvidia misled investors and the public,” California Department of Justice spokesperson Elissa Perez said in a statement.
Last week, before Huang was reinstated, at least two Republican China hawks opposed the idea. Sen. Josh Hawley (R-MO), a rumored potential presidential candidate, told reporters that he would not like to see Huang return to the top post, but would “defer to the board how they want to run their company. If it were me and a guy who just was caught up in a Chinese honeytrap — I think is the technical term for it — I don’t think that I would impose massive security concerns, not just for the company, but for American national security.”
While it was up to the board to decide whether to bring Huang back, Hawley said, “We in Congress ought to be concerned about the American national security implications and I think we should be looking into that.”
Huang “has a serious credibility problem”
House China Committee Chair John Moolenaar (R-MI) said on stage last week at the Aspen Cyber Summit in Washington, D.C., that Huang “has a serious credibility problem, and I don’t believe he would be as effective now as he was before.” His office did not immediately respond to a request for comment after Huang’s reinstatement.
Sitting beside Moolenaar on stage last week, Rep. Greg Stanton (D-AZ) gave his advice to the board: “Don’t do it. Don’t bring it back. And at the very least, slow your roll, because there are so many questions that have to be answered. What else is out there that Jensen Huang has done to put US national security at risk?” Stanton warned that Congress is just beginning to probe what happened here. “There are going to be very serious investigations with very serious ramifications if in fact it is as it seems,” he said. “The company needs to know this ain’t going away for a while. This is a very serious issue.” After news of Huang’s return, Stanton doubled down on calls for investigations.
Other Republicans — some of whom are leaving Congress — notably disagreed with Trump’s jubilance for Huang’s return. “It’s inexplicable to me why they want this guy back as CEO,” retiring Rep. Don Bacon (R-NE) told CNBC. “To me it’s a failure of character.” Sen. Pete Ricketts (R-NE) wrote on X that Huang’s “behavior does not support reinstatement,” and said he must still testify before Congress. “It also doesn’t absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips,” he wrote. Senate Intelligence Committee Chair Tom Cotton (R-AR) wrote on X that he’s not done investigating. “The controversy with Nvidia and Megaspeed is just the tip of the iceberg, and it’s not resolved because Jensen Huang has his job back,” he said. “Congress has much to investigate and we will pass overwhelmingly bipartisan chip export-control bills, including my Chip Security Act, one way or the other.”
“Congress has much to investigate”
Market analysts have been watching and waiting for a Huang comeback since reports that he had assembled a “war room” of allies to help with his possible reinstatement. Not only did Huang cofound one of the world’s most valuable companies and arguably the most important one in the AI boom, but he has personally helped secure hundreds of billions of dollars in infrastructure funding from US financial institutions. Demand for Nvidia chips constantly outpaces supply, and Huang has had the president’s ear for months. Despite all that, though, Huang’s clout seemed like it wouldn’t help him up until the past 24 hours.
Lindsey Stewart, director of institutional insights at Morningstar, wrote in a note that although investors may consider this a “good move given his history of value creation at the company,” questions remain about the best way to provide corporate governance and oversight at such an important company.
Jacob Bourne, an eMarketer analyst specializing in ad tech and consumer technologies, said in a statement to The Verge that it was difficult to gauge “how much protection Trump’s assurances will ultimately provide Nvidia.” And Heather West, head of Eurasia Group’s geo-technology practice, highlighted the fact that Trump recently met with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum. The timing offers Democrats and China hawks “a great deal to work with in 2027 as they begin scrutiny into the administration, potential corruption, and large tech companies[‘] actions here,” said West.
Analysts at Yorkville Ives wrote in a note Monday that they consider Nvidia a $300 stock with Huang and a $225 stock without him, due to his hard-to-replace influence in the sector. They said an interim structure “could not replicate” his supply relationships with TSMC and others, as well as his place in AI industry dealmaking.
“This is a board that reversed itself because the alternative, a founder-less Nvidia at the start of the Rubin cycle with a CEO search running into next year, was the bigger risk to shareholders, and it chose to pair the reversal with the governance architecture investors will want to see around him,” the Yorkville Ives analysts wrote.
Even Trump admits, though, that a true comeback story can’t be called in a single day. “I’ve seen some pretty good comebacks but I’ll tell you, what you have to have for a comeback, really, is longevity,” he told CNBC. He described the pep talk he gave Huang the night before. “I said, ‘You’ve got to promise me one thing. You’ve got the brain, you’ve got everything going, you’ve got to work hard. And if you work hard nobody can beat you.’”
According to Trump, Huang told him, “I’m going to work harder than I’ve ever worked.”

Just days ago, Jensen Huang’s chances of returning as Nvidia CEO looked increasingly slim, at least according to prediction markets. Earlier this month, Huang resigned from the AI hardware giant following reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman alleged to have ties to Chinese intelligence services. As more reports emerged about Huang’s alleged bad behavior, Nvidia’s board insisted it had no plans to reinstate him. By early Sunday morning on the East Coast, traders on Polymarket’s US platform put his chances of returning at just 10 percent. But by Monday, Huang was back in charge.
The swings in Huang’s odds on prediction markets offer a window into how his unlikely comeback unfolded and who saw it coming. The New York Times reported that President Trump played a crucial role in convincing the board to bring Huang back. Traders who paid attention to what Trump and his allies wanted appear to have fared much better than those who did not.
On Sunday evening in Washington, Huang’s odds on Polymarket US jumped six percentage points in just 40 minutes after Trump published a Truth Social missive calling for Huang’s reinstatement. The president said he wanted to help revive the stock market, which had plunged following Huang’s scandal, a sign of Nvidia’s enormous influence over the AI industry and broader US economy.
According to the prediction market intelligence firm Betting Intelligence, odds on both Kalshi and Polymarket’s markets largely tracked with public signals about the likelihood of Huang’s return. They rose when Huang said he was open to returning, fell when the board dismissed the possibility, and climbed again when President Trump threw his support behind the former CEO. But there were several large trades that could not be tied to public developments.
Betting Intelligence and the prediction market forensics firm MSR Decode identified clusters of trades on Huang’s return that did not appear to be driven by news or public commentary. Kalshi and Polymarket declined to comment on whether they are currently investigating potential insider trading in markets related to Huang’s return.
Despite these anomalies, Betting Intelligence CEO Dan Zimmermann says the Huang-related markets showed fewer signs of potentially suspicious activity than usual. “The group that could have known the board’s decision in advance was small. So the market was mostly headline chasers and longshot buyers,” he says.
For traders who profited from Huang’s comeback, the lesson is clear: Don’t discount Trump.
Isaac Rose-Berman, a research and policy fellow at the American Institute for Boys & Men and professional sports bettor, says he made approximately $10,000 wagering on Huang’s return on Kalshi. He placed his trade after the Nvidia chief said on X that he was open to reclaiming his old job. Rose-Berman says that he figured that the board would consider Huang’s return if it looked likely to improve the company’s stock performance. (Never mind the concerns about national security or Huang allegedly threatening employees that he would “pee in your brain.”) “It’s 2026 and Trump is president, scandal schmandal,” Rose-Berman says. “Should’ve bet more.”
A pseudonymous prediction market trader known as Domer tells WIRED he cleared approximately $600,000 by placing an early wager last week on Huang’s return. He wasn’t focused explicitly on Trump’s desires, but he says his understanding of power dynamics ultimately guided his approach. “Boards can be very malleable,” he tells WIRED.
Other prediction market “sharps” say that commentary from Trumpworld was the strongest signal available about Huang’s return. As some bettors noted, there was a notable opportunity for profit after Trump suggested to a PBS NewsHour reporter that Huang would be back in power soon, but before Nvidia officially announced his reinstatement. “The key was looking at Trump’s support and the recent performance of the stock market,” says Kalshi trader Caleb Davies.
Aaron Courtney, a data analyst and cofounder of a prediction market analytics firm, says he took a loss on his Huang position. Looking back, he says his mistake was not paying attention to what Trump and other administration officials said over the weekend. “Trump saying he hoped Nvidia would bring Jensen back would be the clearest signal,” he says.

Mumbai: Indian banks are bracing for rising stress among crop-loan borrowers in drought-hit states, offering loan restructuring and fresh credit while easing off on recoveries.
A deficient monsoon, amid El Niño conditions, has prompted six states to declare drought in certain parts, raising concerns over food inflation and pressure on the rural economy. El Niño, characterised by abnormal warming of waters in the eastern Pacific Ocean, can affect the distribution of rainfall across the Indian subcontinent.
The six states—Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Telangana—had a combined  ₹12 trillion in outstanding agriculture loans as of 31 March, accounting for 11% of their total bank credit, according to Reserve Bank of India (RBI) data. A shortfall in rainfall could hurt crop output and farm incomes, putting repayment capacity under pressure. CareEdge Ratings expects the bad-loan ratio for agricultural loans to rise to 5.5% by March 2028 from 5.1% currently, and potentially cross 6% depending on the extent of stress.
There are concerns that lower crop yields in the coming season could strain rural cash flows, said Vineet Jain, senior director at CareEdge Ratings. Combined with elevated inflation, this could put further pressure on rural households and lead to a deterioration in banks’ asset quality.
Bankers said they are rolling out measures to ease the burden on rural borrowers, but have yet to see significant uptake.
“The policies are ready, following discussions at state-level bankers’ committee (SLBC) meetings, but so far not many borrowers have availed themselves of these measures,” said the chief executive of a large public sector bank.
The banker, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said borrowers were likely to approach banks eventually, but were still assessing the extent of the impact on their finances. The banker added that, under the applicable restructuring framework, these loans would continue to be classified as standard, rather than being downgraded to non-performing assets, as can happen with other loan restructurings.
Measures
State Bank of India (SBI), the country’s largest lender, has identified ₹10,000 crore worth of loans as a potential pool for restructuring. Chairman C.S. Setty told analysts on 3 November that past experience showed that relatively few borrowers come forward to seek restructuring. SBI’s agriculture loan portfolio across India stood at ₹4.5 trillion in the second quarter of FY27, up 22.6% from a year earlier.
Over the past couple of months, bankers have met at state-level forums, in the presence of regulatory and government officials, to work out support measures for distressed borrowers. At a meeting of the Maharashtra State-Level Bankers’ Committee on 6 October, for instance, lenders decided to restructure existing short-term crop-production loans, reschedule instalments and extend fresh credit, according to a letter dated 12 October.
In Karnataka, bankers held a special meeting on 10 September to discuss similar measures. They were given until 9 January to implement them.
“The chairperson gave a strong directive that this is not a year for harsh recovery measures or creating panic among farmers,” according to a copy of the meeting minutes seen by Mint. The meeting was chaired by Uma Mahadevan, additional chief secretary and development commissioner, Government of Karnataka.
Bad-loan ratio
CareEdge Ratings’ Jain said that, since the stress stems from a natural calamity, banks can restructure agricultural loans in districts where the state government has declared drought. They have until February 2027 to use this window, he said. As a result, the impact is unlikely to show up in the March 2027 numbers.
CareEdge expects the agricultural bad-loan ratio to improve from 5.1% in September to around 4.7-4.8% by March 2027, supported by growth in outstanding loans and write-offs of bad loans. “However, it will increase by March 2028 to 5.5% and could even cross 6%, depending on the stress,” Jain said.
Analysts at BMI, a unit of Fitch Solutions, said in a note on 4 November that India’s weakest monsoon since 2015 would increase downside risks to agricultural loan quality. Agricultural lending remains the principal source of additional credit risk, the note said.
Bankers, however, remain optimistic that they can manage the impact of the drought. Rajneesh Karnatak, chief executive of Bank of India, said the lender’s September-quarter financials showed little impact on asset quality. Its agriculture loan portfolio stood at ₹1.2 trillion as of 30 September, up 16.3% from a year earlier.
“We feel that with the kind of robust systems that the bank has built, all the banks have built, and the agility with which we are working, we are confident that we’ll be able to tide over these headwinds,” Karnatak told analysts on 23 October.

New Delhi: India has shortlisted 11 candidates for its top drug regulator post, advancing the selection process for the regulator of its $60 billion pharmaceutical sector, as the government steps up scrutiny of drug quality, including medicines meant for export.
The Union health ministry has shortlisted the candidates from 28 applicants for interviews, according to two officials and a document reviewed by Mint. The shortlist has been cleared by a three-member screening panel under revised recruitment rules that expanded eligibility for the post of Drugs Controller General of India (DCGI).
The post falls vacant on 1 March 2027, when incumbent Dr Rajeev Singh Raghuvanshi’s second one-year contractual term ends.
The selection comes as India, the world’s pharmacy for low-cost generics and vaccines, faces renewed scrutiny of its drug-quality standards. Over the past few years, Indian-manufactured cough syrups have been linked to more than 140 deaths globally, including in Gambia, Uzbekistan and Cameroon, following contamination with toxic industrial solvents such as Diethylene Glycol (DEG) and Ethylene Glycol (EG).
The government is also sending a team to the World Health Organization to learn best practices and better align domestic drug inspections with global standards.
The shortlisted candidates will now be sent to the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) for final interviews. The final appointment will be cleared by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC), one of the officials cited earlier said.
The DCGI heads the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO), which is responsible for ensuring the safety and efficacy of drugs, medical devices and clinical trials.
Queries sent to the spokesperson of the health ministry and DCGI office on Saturday remained unanswered until press time.
Wider pool, broader expertise
The 28 applicants included officials from the CDSCO, the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC), state drug-control departments and academic institutions such as AIIMS New Delhi, PGIMER Chandigarh, NIPER Ahmedabad, and IIT-BHU.
Applications also came from the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) in Lucknow, the National Dope Testing Laboratory, the National Centre for Disease Control, an autonomous state medical college in Uttar Pradesh and the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
The revised Recruitment Rules, 2026, notified in April, expanded the pool of eligible candidates. In a first, the framework allows candidates with master’s degrees in non-pharmacy engineering disciplines, including mechanical, electrical and computer science, to apply alongside those with degrees in pharmacy, chemistry, life sciences and medicine. A doctorate is considered an added advantage.
Applicants must have at least 15 years of practical experience in drug manufacturing, testing, clinical trials or medical-device oversight. The 1 August 2026 recruitment advertisement said the post would be filled on a deputation or short-term contract basis for up to five years, with an upper age limit of 58 years.
“Once the UPSC conducts the final interviews and recommends a candidate, the final appointment will be cleared by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC),” the official cited earlier said.
“Alongside supportive government policies and recent Goods and Services Tax (GST) rationalizations aiding the sector, achieving long-term goals requires shifting from volume to value and maintaining regulatory continuity. It is not about the person; it is about that position. Whoever comes into that place has to ensure that the industry, regulator, and academicians all work together—that integration is more important than anything else,” Viranchi Shah, national spokesperson, Indian Drug Manufacturers’ Association (IDMA).

Black travelers on Route 66 weren't welcome at most gas stations — except this one
During the Jim Crow Era, Black families traveling Route 66, the historic highway that ran more than 2,000 miles from Chicago to Los Angeles, needed to carry food and gas with them. Most restaurants, gas stations and motels wouldn't serve them.
But there was one place they were guaranteed to find respite: a small, family-owned business just east of Oklahoma City that offered fuel, food and a place to stop for the night. The Threatt Filling Station, according to the National Trust for Historic Preservation, was the only known Black-owned and operated gas station along the famous Mother Road.
"Grandpa took care of whatever they needed to have," said Linda Fisher, the granddaughter of the station's founder, Allen Threatt Sr. Her family still owns the station and the 150 acres around it.
"If they didn't have any food, they fed them," she said. "If they needed some kind of shelter or blankets or those types of things, Grandpa and Grandma made sure they got those kinds of things."
Threatt moved from Alabama to the farming community of Luther, Okla., in the early 1900s as part of the Great Migration. His father had been born into slavery, and Threatt and his wife, Alberta, seeking stability and refuge, wanted their own farm.
At the time, Oklahoma was a place where Black migrants could own land and form their own towns. Between 1865 and 1920, Black Americans settled more than 50 "all-Black" municipalities in Oklahoma, the largest number of any state.
But Oklahoma also had its issues — by the time of the Great Depression, many of those all-Black towns had ceased to exist. And there was a rise in "sundown towns": all-white communities that warned non-white people to get out before dark, or they would face violence or police harassment. There was a sundown town on either side of the filling station during the Jim Crow era, Fisher said.
But at the Threatt Filling Station, "everyone was welcome," Fisher said.
The building, which closed to the public in the 1970s, is now on the National Register of Historic Places.
A century of welcome
Allen Threatt Sr. built the original filling station in 1915, when he started to notice people driving by a corner of his property on what was then the Ozark Trail.
In 1926, Route 66 was founded, and the trickle of cars became a steady stream. When the old wooden building burned down, Threatt replaced it with a charming sandstone one, built like a small, welcoming house.
Eventually, the station and the property surrounding it became a community hub. There were dances in the restaurant next door, social club meetings, barbecues. Occasionally, players from the Negro Leagues would have a game on the baseball diamond.
Allen and Alberta Threatt had 11 living children, and a couple of them took over the running of the station in the 1950s.
But the building of the Interstate Highway System, launched under the Eisenhower administration, led to dwindling traffic on Route 66, and by the mid-'70s, the station had closed.
A half-century later later, the building was derelict. In 2021, the National Trust for Historic Preservation listed the station as one of America's 11 Most Endangered Historic Places.
But hope was around the corner: A few years earlier, a trio of Allen Threatt Sr.'s grandchildren decided to restore the property. Now, thanks to nonprofit grants and a lot of cousin elbow grease, the filling station has a restored exterior.
Ceramic Conoco gas pumps from the 1940s stand proudly outside; new signs inside detail the history of the family, the gas station and Route 66, and visitors can talk to the Threatts themselves and buy a T-shirt.
Eventually, the family is planning to build an RV park, a restaurant and perhaps even a new baseball diamond.
"We're all standing on Grandpa's shoulders — Grandpa and Grandma's shoulders," said Edward Threatt, another grandchild of Allen Threatt Sr. who is one of the leaders of the restoration.
"We have this property today because of Grandpa, and so we represent him, we represent our mothers, our fathers. And we're just trying to do them proud, that's all."
Broadcast and digital story edited by Steven Drummond; audio mixed by Chloee Weiner. Photo editing by Emily Bogle.

- Alpha is a Fisch attribute that increases a fish's sell value by 2.5x.
- It gives fish a unique look, making them blue with a special glowing effect.
- There is a 0.1% chance to get an Alpha fish, but it increases to 0.5% with the Alpha Anomaly modifier event.
Alpha is a rare fish attribute, similar to Shiny and Sparkling, in Fisch. It gives fish a unique blue color and increases their sell value by 2.5x. It has a low chance of occurring naturally, but you can improve your odds by fishing during an exclusive anomaly event.
Fisch Alpha Attribute Multiplier Value
Alpha is a special attribute that works just like Shiny & Sparkling but has a higher 2.5x sell value multiplier. It also changes the fish’s appearance, making it glow blue with a blue charge circling it.
The Bestiary records the date of your first Alpha catch for each fish entry, but you will first need to complete your Shiny and Sparkling bestiaries. Once you do, only then will the Alpha bestiary count at the bottom unlock. It hasn’t for me, because I only have around 50% Sparkling and Shiny fish in total.
How to Get Alpha Fish in Fisch
There are three ways to get an Alpha fish in Fisch:
- Natural Fishing: There is a 0.1% chance to get the Alpha attribute when catching a fish.
- Appraisal: You have a 0.1% chance to get the Alpha attribute when appraising a fish in Fisch.
- Alpha Anomaly: If you fish or appraise your fish during an Alpha Anomaly, it gives you an extra 0.4% chance to catch Alpha fish. Your total Alpha chance increases to 0.5%.
How to Start the Alpha Anomaly in Fisch
The Alpha Anomaly works like other modifier events in Fisch. It has a chance to appear after the server’s modifier cooldown ends, at the start of a new day or new night.
Like other modifier events, improve your chances of triggering Alpha Anomaly by following these steps:
- Unlike weather events in Fisch, modifier events usually roll after a random cooldown of about 45 to 50 minutes. This can trigger the Alpha Anomaly when the previous modifier timer ends.
- Avoid using modifier totems like Shiny, Sparkling, or Mutation Totems in Fisch, as they might trigger another modifier that can reset the timer.
- Use Sundial totems to change the day and night cycle. Alpha Anomaly has a 33% chance to spawn at the start of a new day and a 20% chance to spawn at the start of nighttime.
This guide should help you obtain the Alpha attribute in Fisch. Moreover, have you unlocked the Soulseamed Felina rod yet? Let us know in the comments below.
What is the chance of catching an Alpha fish?
You have a 0.1% chance of getting an Alpha attribute fish while fishing or appraising a fish.
How often can the Alpha Anomaly spawn?
Modifier events roll every 45 to 50 minutes in a server. Once the cycle ends, Alpha Anomaly has a 33% chance and a 20% chance to spawn at the start of daytime and nighttime, respectively.

England levelled the T20 international series at 1-1 with an eight-wicket win over Australia on Tuesday, powered by a 151-run opening stand between Aneurin Donald and Phil Salt.
Set 185 to win, the visitors dominated from the first over, with Donald and Salt taking the target apart at a rapid pace.
Donald hit 85 from 32 balls, with nine sixes and four fours, before Riley Meredith dismissed him with England on 151-1. Salt scored 58 off 30 balls, including four sixes and five fours, until Ben Dwarshuis took a superb one-handed caught-and-bowled to end his innings.
ALSO READ: AUS vs ENG Highlights, 2nd T20I: England beats Australia by eight wickets
Captain Harry Brook (10 not out) and Tom Banton (26 not out) finished the job comfortably. Banton hit the winning six as England reached 188-2 in 13.1 overs, with 41 balls remaining.
“That was unbelievable (Donald-Salt partnership),” Brook said. “It was explosive to say the least.
“Those two put on an absolute clinic. They should be very proud of their performance.”
Australia captain Mitchell Marsh had chosen to bat after his team’s three-wicket win in Saturday’s series opener. England fought back early, though, after an Australian opener struck successive sixes at the start of the innings.
Marsh gave a return catch to bowler Henry Crocombe (2-40), and Sam Curran (2-29) dismissed Jake Fraser-McGurk for 27. England debutant James Coles then ran out Sam Harper with a diving underarm throw.
Spinner Adil Rashid (1-26) tightened the squeeze as Australia fell to 84-5 after 11 overs.
Nikhil Chaudhary led a fightback with 45 from 35 balls, adding 49 with Joel Davies (39). Dwarshuis then gave the innings late momentum by hitting Curran for three straight sixes, and Australia ended on 184-8.
“182, I thought we were in the game,” Marsh said. “Surface got good at the end, but hats off, sometimes good balls were going 40 rows back.
“I think we were four down at the end of the powerplay, we probably didn’t give ourselves a chance. But we came off the ground thinking we were 10-15 over par, shows how much I know.”

We weren't able to confirm, as of this writing, precisely how many barrels of lead azide would be exploded.
In mid-November, a rumor spread online that the U.S. Army had plans to set off two detonations to destroy an old cache of lead azide — a highly explosive compound — in Middletown, Iowa, on Nov. 20.
"The Army found 68 barrels of the explosive that had been stored at the plant for more than 20 years," one Facebook post read (archived). "Lead azide becomes more unstable as it ages and can detonate with slight movement or friction, making it unsafe to move off site."
The claim spread across other platforms, with several Snopes readers also contacting us for answers.
In short, the claim is true. Here's what we know:
Army confirms explosions will take place
The Iowa Army Ammunition Plant launched a campaign to inform the public about the upcoming explosions, including an open house on Oct. 15 and a notice (archived) on Nov. 15 warning people in the affected area to evacuate and inviting residents to shelter at the Armed Forces Reserve Center during the explosions if needed.
In a document titled "Keeping Our Community Safe," the Army described how plans to reduce harm from the explosion by using specialized water misters and cleaning and removing affected soil and debris once the operation ceases.
(U.S. Army)
The public warnings issued by the Army to residents in the area were as follows:
- Consider avoiding the affected area.
- If you are inside of the affected areas, avoid outdoor air by staying indoors.
- Keep windows and doors closed.
- If it is safe to do so, set heating and cooling systems to "recirculate" to minimize outdoor air exposure and maximize indoor air filtration until the plume passes by your community.
- Avoid unnecessary travel through impacted areas.
- After the US Army determines the air exposure period has ended, consider cleaning indoor and outdoor surfaces such as play surfaces for children and windowsills.
- If your car was parked outside, consider washing your car at a car wash to minimize your contact with potentially exposed surfaces.
Is the circulated 'blast zone' map accurate?
In the circulated map shown in the Facebook post above, the blast zone appears to stretch approximately 100 miles northeast from the blast site. We compared this map to maps the Army released ahead of the planned detonations and found they aligned.
(Facebook user Live Storm Chasers and U.S. Army)
As Nov. 20 draws closer, the Army's maps will be updated. Residents in the area were encouraged to regularly check for updates.
What is lead azide and how did it get there?
According to the Environmental Protection Agency, lead azide is a "hazardous waste that exhibits the characteristic of reactivity (energetic) and exhibits the characteristic of toxicity for lead." In a public notice (archived) Nov. 16, the EPA wrote:
The recrystallization of the stored lead azide has increased the material's sensitivity to friction and shock, and disturbing the containers of lead azide could create an unacceptable risk of unintentional detonation. The Army's evaluation of a range of potential alternatives for the treatment of lead azide culminated in the secretary of the Army selecting in-place, controlled, intentional detonation for the treatment of lead azide.
The material is used to initiate munitions, according to a Q&A document the Army published.
It's unclear precisely how the lead azide stores came to be stored at that underground location. While a number of media outlets reported that 68 barrels would be detonated, we were unable to confirm that amount. We contacted the Army seeking more context and information about the history of the lead azide stores and will update this story if we receive a response.
In March, the Army announced that experts were conducting a safety review for the "safe removal of a chemical compound currently at the plant."
On Nov. 17, local ABC affiliate KCRG reported that local activists were planning a "peaceful demonstration" against the planned detonations.
Group organizers were reportedly demanding:
- An immediate halt to the Nov. 20 lead azide detonation, at minimum until affected communities have had an adequate opportunity to review the risks and alternatives.
- Full transparency regarding the potential environmental and public health consequences.
- Independent environmental experts to review the proposed disposal method and evaluate safer alternatives.
- A comprehensive plan for independent air, soil, and surface testing in potentially affected communities.
- A commitment to clean up and remediate any lead contamination resulting from this operation, at no cost to affected residents and property owners.

Amid mounting pressure from different quarters on the Madurai district administration for and against lighting of lamp on the newly identified Deepathoon atop Thirupparankundram hillock on Karthigai Deepam day on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), the Madurai City Police brought the entire hillock under a thick security blanket on Monday. The Supreme Court had permitted the lamp to be lit at the newly identified Deepathoon as a “one-time arrangement”.
The police declared areas around Thirupparankundram a “red zone” and prohibited flying of drones and unmanned aerial vehicles on Monday and Tuesday. Hundreds of police personnel have been deployed around the hillock that houses the Subramania Swamy Temple to prevent any unauthorised person gaining access to the hilltop where Deepathoon is located.
Madurai Collector Nishant Krishna promulgated prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) across the entire district on Monday evening, banning public assemblies and barring anyone from climbing the Thirupparankundram Hill ahead of the festival.
A police officer said more than 2,000 personnel of the Tamil Nadu Special Police, drawn from different districts, would be deployed in and around Thiruppankundram.
Parties blame TVK-led government
Certain political parties, including the BJP and outfits such as Hindu Munnani and Hindu Dharma Parishad, have criticised the State government for filing a review petition against the Supreme Court order. They said the TVK-led government was only toeing the previous DMK government’s line. The DMK government had refused to follow a similar order issued by the Madras High Court during Karthigai Deepam in 2025.
Hindu Dharma Parishad representatives warned the district administration that any attempt to go against the Supreme Court order would result in contempt proceedings against the Collector.
Though the Supreme Court has said it will be a one-time measure and should not been seen as a precedent, some political parties and organisations are representing to the Subramania Swamy Temple Devasthanam against permitting the lighting of the lamp on Deepathoon. An advocate, Vanjinathan, wondered whether the TVK government was allowing the Sangh Parivar to go ahead with its “conspiracy” to turn Thirupparankundram into another “Ayodhya”.
Peaceful demonstration
Madanallinakka Kootaippu, a body advocating for religious harmony, staged a peaceful demonstration in Madurai to protect the “Tamils’ unity” in Thirupparankundram by allowing the lampt to be lit only near the Utchipillaiyar Temple as had been the tradition for decades. Political parties, including the DMK, the VCK, the Congress, the Left parties, the SDPI, the TMMK, and the MNK, took part in the protest.
The police fear that whatever be the government’s decision, it will cause discontent among one section of the people, leading to an untoward situation. A police officer recalled that hundreds of Hindus, who were disappointed in 2025 because the lamp was not lit on Deepathoon, had sneaked into the Thirupparankundram temple and created tension after the Karthigai Deepam festival.
“Despite the presence of hundreds of police, the devotees from far and near managed to get into the temple and staged a protest,” he told The Hindu.
The police fear that this time more devotees and workers of Hindu organisations are likely to throng the temple premises, which would usually attract thousands of devotees for the grand event.
Police pickets posted at entrances
As a precautionary measure, the police have posted pickets at both entrances to the hilltop where devotees offer prayers at the Kasiviswanathar Temple as well as Sikandar Badushah Dargah.
The police said no one should fly drones atop the hillock, Girivala roads, and the entrance of Thirupparankundram so far as the 16-Pillar Mandapam, and the foothills. Police permission would be mandatory for flying drones for any inevitable work and violators would face legal action, they warned.

India A will look to seal its place in the semifinals of the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 when it takes on the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in its final Group B fixture in Doha on Tuesday, November 24.
The Tilak Varma-led side suffered a 48-run defeat to Pakistan A in its previous outing, missing the opportunity to secure an early qualification. However, a commanding 306-run victory over Nepal in its tournament opener has left India with a healthy net run rate and several possible routes into the last four.
India currently sits second in Group B with two points from two matches, behind Pakistan A, which has already qualified after winning both its fixtures. Nepal is third with two points, while the UAE is bottom without a win.
The top two teams from each group will qualify for the semi-finals, scheduled for November 26 and 27.
India’s net run rate of +2.580 is its biggest advantage heading into the final round of Group B matches. The 306-run victory over Nepal has given it a considerable cushion over its closest qualification rival.
India A vs UAE: What does India need to qualify?
Scenario 1: India beats UAE and Pakistan A beats Nepal
This is India’s most straightforward route into the semifinals.
A victory over the UAE will take India to four points. If Pakistan A also beats Nepal, India will finish second with four points, while Nepal and the UAE will be unable to catch it.
India will qualify alongside Pakistan A.
Scenario 2: India beats UAE and Nepal beats Pakistan A
India will still have a strong chance of qualifying.
A Nepal victory will take it to four points, while Pakistan A, India A and Nepal will all finish with four points.
In that situation, the final positions will be determined by net run rate. India currently has a significant advantage over both Pakistan A (+1.090) and Nepal (-2.461).
Scenario 3: India loses to UAE and Pakistan A beats Nepal
India’s qualification hopes will remain alive even after a defeat.
Pakistan A will finish with six points, while India, Nepal and the UAE will all have two points.
The second semifinal position will then be decided by net run rate among the three teams.
India’s current NRR of +2.580 gives it a significant advantage over Nepal (-2.461) and the UAE (-2.061).
Scenario 4: India loses to UAE and Nepal beats Pakistan A
This is the one result combination that will eliminate India A.
Nepal will finish with four points, joining Pakistan A, which already has four points and has qualified.
India will remain on two points, irrespective of its net run rate, and will be knocked out alongside the UAE.
What matches remain in Group B?
Both remaining Group B fixtures will be played on November 24.
India A vs UAE: 11:30 AM IST
Pakistan A vs Nepal: 3:30 PM IST
When are the Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 semifinals?
The semifinals are scheduled for November 26 and 27, with the final set to take place on November 29.
