I return to my room as my mother-in-law leaves for her office in the building adjacent to our home. I am about to start my bath when I hear a series of explosions, as of firecrackers, but different. I freeze. Someone comes pounding frantically on my bathroom door. It is Ongmu, the children’s nanny, crying hysterically. I fling open the door, my heart thumping. She is gesticulating wildly, speechlessly, towards the garden.
I run along the path leading to Akbar Road. I see the white Ambassador car slowly moving towards the same path. I hesitate. I stop, heart in my mouth. Dread, panic, fear. I feel suffocated. I can’t breathe. I am about to collapse. No, no, I can’t. I have to walk to the car. I see her being carried into it. I understand; I scream.
I’m in the car now, crouching on the floor, facing her … Blood – blood on her sari, blood on her chest. Her large eyes are wide open; her face wears a surprised expression. She doesn’t move. I attempt to speak to her, to call out, “Mummy, Mummy”, but no word comes out. I try again; she doesn’t reply.
Her aides are in the front of the car, screaming. Heavy, slow traffic, the car barely moves, it has no siren. One red light, then another. Then the hospital. The gate isn’t opening. Chaos. We are stopped; someone looks through the window in a questioning attitude. They let us in.
We reach the emergency department, teeming with people. We are stopped again, not allowed in, we have to wait for our turn. Someone calls out to the driver, signals him to move forward. They identify us; she is placed on a trolley. We are led somewhere – an operation theatre? They ask me to follow. I’m taken to a room nearby. No, no, I want to stay by her, I insist. I want to know. I have to see. They don’t reply; they are immersed in their emergency procedures.
I feel confused, lost … I don’t recognise anyone there. I’m shivering under my dressing gown. I feel scared, my mind is racing. Where is Rajiv? I try to remember. I can’t, I can’t. The children, yes, they’re in school; they must be brought home. Oh God, no, no. Let them be safe, let Rajiv be safe … Whom do I tell, whom do I speak to? I sense someone in the room. I don’t know who it is. I try to speak, to put some words together; nothing comes out. “There’s blood all over her clothes,” someone says. Some clothes are brought in for me. I am helped into them in a nearby closet.
Hours go by, agonising hours. More people come in and crowd around. I signal a question to the doctor; he shakes his head. I understand, yes, I understand. I break into sobs, uncontrollably. Someone tries to calm me. I feel numb, cold.
At two in the afternoon of 31 October 1984, Indira Gandhi was declared dead. I was driven home to collect some clothes for her body to be changed into. On the way, a group of men tried to stop our car, banging on its windows. They were angry, shouting something I couldn’t understand.
At home, the children, Rahul and Priyanka, rushed to my arms in tears. When they had been abruptly picked up from school by black-uniformed commandos, they sensed a catastrophe. Once home, they saw some of the staff sobbing. They asked question after question. “Where’s Mama?” “Why have we been brought home?” “Where’s Papa?” “What’s happened?” “Where’s Dadi?” “You aren’t telling us the truth!” My friends Nina and Sterre had been with them, trying to calm them down, not knowing what to say to them. I wanted to sit with them and hug them, to break the news to them gently, but I was unable to – I had to go back; Rajiv was coming to the hospital.
Rajiv had been in West Bengal at a political rally when his cavalcade was stopped by a police patrol. He was told there was a message from Delhi to say he should rush back – a serious accident had taken place. He was driven to the helipad, from where he flew to Calcutta and then to Delhi. He’d heard on a BBC bulletin that Mrs Gandhi was wounded and in a grave condition. Nobody told him directly that his mother was no more, but he understood.
He landed at 3.30pm and was driven straight to the hospital. He walked in with other people, and I remember longing to be left alone with him for a moment at least. We held each other, and as he spoke to me, it sunk in that he was saying something I didn’t want to hear. “I have been asked … They want me to be sworn in as prime minister.”
I felt as if a knife had been plunged right into my heart. I felt a pounding in my chest, a rage welling up deep inside me. I was about to explode. I attempted to hold it in. “You have been asked to? How dare they ask? How dare they? Who are they? Why you, why does it have to be you? Why did you allow them to ask you? No, it cannot be; this time it’s not going to be!” Seized by utter pain and anguish, soaked in perspiration, I felt like throwing up. I wanted to scream, to ask for help. “Someone please help me put an end to this.”
I burst out crying, pleading, begging him with folded hands, “No, no, you can’t think of it. You have to stop them, you must refuse, you must say no – for the children’s sake, for yourself. You can’t do this to us. They will kill you; they will kill you, too!” I cried out. He replied, “They will kill me anyway.”
We brought my mother-in-law home. The dining room had been emptied out, and we laid her body down on the floor, her feet pointing south as Hindu custom decrees. The same evening at around 6.30pm, Rajiv was sworn in as prime minister of India. I was too broken to even register what was happening around me. His mother lay there, her body pierced with more than 30 bullet holes. I knew, I knew it then in my heart: Rajiv’s path would lead to the same end.

EXCLUSIVE: Veteran execs from the media, entertainment and brand sectors have teamed up to launch an all-purpose advisory coalition, we can reveal.
The Unlabelled Alliance comprises ex-UTA and Fremantle branded chief Sam Glynne, 7Wonder founder and TV producer Liza Abbott, Somethin’ Else director and audio industry veteran Steve Ackerman, Gleam Futures founder and creator economy talent manager Dom Smales and Little Dot Studios co-founder Selma Turajlic.
Each has more than 20 years’ experience in their field, and they will look to bring their particular expertise to the advisory, which will look at helping media companies transform, innovate and scale by unlocking the value of their IP and forming partnerships with other players in digital, audio, talent and the brand space.
This will include monetizing content; repurposing catalog, licenses and distribution models; digital strategy; how to turn brands into partners, not simply sponsors; working with creators and talent; and backing the right digital-first ideas.
Watch on Deadline
Each member of the Unlabelled Alliance will continue to run their own businesses and ventures, and provide tailored advice and support to clients – meaning they can form different combinations and find solutions based on the company.
The coalition is targeting broadcasters, studios, distributors, publishers, music companies, talent agencies, production companies and brands, and is pitching its offer as “experience-based solutions without the burden of fixed overheads.” As such they’re presenting the advisory as a “deliberately lean, plug-in model” that engages only as long as a problem requires.
Their rationale for the alliance is that the industry is not simply changing, but “fracturing and rebuilding itself in a completely different shape.” They note that broadcaster commission budgets are shrinking in many cases, while the creator economy is growing and formats often shift across mediums and platforms. The plan for the business has been in the works for some time, with a website now up and running, and we understand several deals are set to conclude.
“We came together as a group, first as friends and then with a shared vision of using our experience to future-proof the industry that we’ve grown up in,” the Unlabelled Alliance co-founders said in a statement.
“We built our careers in traditional media and went on to revolutionise it from the inside out: building and scaling businesses, pioneering digital-first content, creating new models for talent and re-imagining legacy IP potential. We know the pain points because we’ve been there. Our aim is your innovation and growth.”
They added they would be a “hands-on and results-driven advisory team of seasoned specialists, helping C-suites, boards, founders and investors work out what is stopping them scaling and delivering real, smart and swift solutions.”
Abbott will provide IP, studios and transformational and operational infrastructure advice. She was most recently the Chief Content Officer at The Earthshot Prize, Prince William’s environmental initiative. Prior to that, she was COO of Unscripted at Fremantle, overseeing Thames, Talkback, Boundless and Shotglass. She was co-founder of 7Wonder, the UK production joint venture of Maverick Television and Australia’s Seven Network that’s now part of Banijay. Abbott has also held senior roles at Maverick, ITV Studios, IMG and the BBC.
Ackerman plans to offer audio, podcasting and content strategy advice. He is known as one of radio giant and multimedia production pioneer Somethin’ Else’s early directors, and led the company up to its sale to Sony Music Entertainment, at which point he became EVP and Head of Global Podcasts for the Sony. He is now a non-exec director of The Podcast Show and subscription platform SupaPass.
Glynne is the branded entertainment and IP strategy expert. She founded and was head of UTA’s EMEA Entertainment and Culture Marketing business, and worked as Global SVP of Branded Entertainment at Fremantle, working across 30 territories. Prior to that, she ran Renault TV and set up and ran The Audi Channel for All3Media and BBH. She’s also a Cannes Lions judge.
Smales, considered by many the architect of the creator economy and influencer world in Europe, will focus on talent and the creator economy solutions. He’s known for leading Gleam Futures, the early digital-first talent management business he founded in 2010. In 2021, he exited for Dentsu and now runs WinnieWood, a creator economy group that spans talent management, entertainment IP, commerce, tech and investments, and is a co-founder of creator-led entertainment producer GloMotion Studios.
Turajlic will handle digital transformation and entrepreneurship. She is known as co-founder of Little Dot Studios alongside the late Andy Taylor. The business, which now has well over 500 staff, has been singled out as a key pillar in growth for Banijay, which added Little Dot to its ranks through its acquisition of All3 this year. Turajlic also had senior roles at All3, Sony Pictures Television an Celador International, and is now a venture builder and angel investor with Alma Angels.

Former Sequoia Capital India investor Sudhanshu Mishra has launched an agentic AI startup called Demi.AI in the US, seeking to build an AI assistant that can anticipate users' requirements and complete work before being explicitly instructed. Mishra announced the launch of Demi's invite-only beta earlier today on social media. He positioned it as an “AI assistant that lives on your Mac, learns how you work, and does the work before you ask”. Demi’s other cofounder is Mishra’s college roommate Logan Ford and currently employs about 10 people. Demi was set up in June 2025. Mishra was earlier associated with Sequoia Capital as an investor. He worked on early-stage investments, primarily leading the firm's crypto-focused efforts. He subsequently joined Paradigm, a crypto-focused investment firm, as an investment partner. In his launch announcement, Mishra said the idea behind Demi was to reduce the effort users currently need to put into making AI tools useful, including setting up workflows, providing context and figuring out which tasks to delegate. Unlike conventional AI assistants that largely respond to individual prompts, Demi aims to continuously build an understanding of users' work and identify tasks that need attention. How Does Demi Work? Demi builds context from users' meetings, connected applications and even their computer screens to understand ongoing projects, conversations and work patterns. Based on this context, it tracks commitments, deadlines and recurring tasks, and proactively surfaces reminders or prepares the next steps. For instance, if a user promises to share a document during a meeting, Demi can identify the commitment, locate relevant information and prepare a follow-up email. The platform can also handle repetitive administrative work, including drafting email responses, preparing meeting briefs, capturing meeting notes, updating customer relationship management (CRM) systems and tracking customer follow-ups. The agentic platform then executes these tasks either through its cloud-based computer or natively on a user's Mac through their browser. Moreover, users do not need to create custom workflows or write instructions for individual skills to get started. The platform still retains a human approval layer and messages, commitments and important changes to records are presented to users for approval before they are executed. According to its website, its individual paid plan starts at $25 per month, while team pricing is customised. Agentic AI has emerged as the biggest buzz word across the global tech ecosystem with most enterprises and individuals exploring ways to automate their workflows using AI. According to Grand View Research, the global enterprise agentic AI market is projected to reach $24.5 Bn by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 46.2%. Investor interest in agentic AI is also accelerating as a new crop of startups look to automate workflows across varied enterprise applications. For instance, Sol Foundry, founded by former CRED executives, raised $4 Mn from General Catalyst, Nexus Venture Partners and others in September this year to build a proactive AI assistant that acts on commitments made over email.

A suspected Ukrainian drone attack caused an explosion on a Russian warship docked at the naval base in the Libyan port city of Benghazi, Libyan officials have said.
The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy warship, and ignited a fire at the naval base, they said. Several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship from a base run by Ukrainian forces in western Libya, according to an initial investigation into the attack. At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two hit the warship, the officials told the Associated Press.
The officials were affiliated with the self-styled Libyan National Army, which controls eastern and southern Libya.
There was no immediate reaction from Russian authorities, and no immediate claim of responsibility for the strike, but it comes as Ukrainian forces have stepped up their long-range barrages against Russia far beyond the frontlines.
Authorities in divided Libya’s east said in a statement that the vessel had stopped at Benghazi port to refuel and resupply on its way back to Russia, under maritime cooperation agreements between the two countries.
Two medical sources told Reuters no deaths had been reported, but there were injuries. The number and nationalities of those injured are not yet known.
In a separate attack, another sea drone hit a commercial vessel off the port of Benghazi on Sunday evening, Libyan military sources told Reuters.
The eastern-based Libyan authority said port and naval base facilities, including warehouses, were safe and that normal operations would resume once the fire was brought under control and the site secured.
It condemned the suspected attack as a violation of Libya’s sovereignty and a threat to maritime safety, saying it would take legal and diplomatic measures against anyone found responsible. “The Libyan government will not allow Libyan ports, territory or territorial waters to be turned into an arena for settling scores or exporting international conflicts,” it said.
The specialist website Naval News also identified the ship attacked as the Merkury, a Russian corvette – the smallest class of warship, smaller than a frigate – and said it was almost certainly destroyed.
HI Sutton, a naval analyst, said the attack was probably conducted by sea drones, after a photograph of one emerged apparently taken off the Libyan coast. The drone, he said, “is also likely the type used in the subsequent attack”.
If it is confirmed that Ukraine has been able to blow up or seriously damage a Russian warship in Benghazi, it would represent one of its most successful naval strikes during the almost five-year war.
But it also represents a risky extension of the fighting far beyond eastern Europe, in an incident that could affect civilians in another continent and the working of the port.
A small unit of Ukrainian special forces operatives has been based at Misrata, western Libya, and is believed to have coordinated drone attacks on Russian tankers and transport ships in the past year.
Initial reports and footage suggest the Merkury was struck from above, potentially by a drone, launched no more than a few kilometres away from the target in port.
Russia is close to the Benghazi authorities that control eastern Libya. It uses the port, which has a growing importance since it lost bases in Syria, to supply Russian mercenary forces in Africa and as a base in the Mediterranean.
Separately, a fire onboard a Russian cargo ship that was struck by drones in the Baltic Sea continued to smoulder on Sunday, Finland’s border guard said, with emergency services from Finland, Russia and Estonia working together to put out the blaze.
The Finnish military said the strike on the Sparta II on Saturday was probably carried out by Ukraine and that the vessel later drifted into Finnish waters, where it remained at anchor. The 16 crew members were evacuated on to a nearby Russian ship. One crew member was slightly injured.
On Sunday, visible flames had been put out, with operations focusing on cooling down the containers and stabilising the vessel, Finnish authorities said.
The ship, bound for the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, had been damaged in international waters west of Russia’s Gogland Island, Finland’s defence forces said, corroborating an account by Russian officials.
Kyiv has sent waves of military drones towards the Leningrad region on Russia’s north-west coast this year, including some that strayed into the airspace of nearby Baltic countries, leading to fears that the war was spilling on to Nato territory.
The risk of further attacks in the Gulf of Finland, a narrow arm of the Baltic Sea, could not be ruled out, Ivo Värk, the Estonian navy commander, told the public broadcaster ERR on Sunday.
Finland’s military said last week it had detected a strike on a Russian warship in the same area during Ukrainian drone attacks.
Reuters and the Associated Press contributed to this report

Tarkowski's first Premier League red ruins Moyes' night - was it deserved?
- Published
It had been some run for Everton captain James Tarkowski.
Prior to Monday night, the defender had received 74 yellow cards in the Premier League but had never been sent off - a top-flight record.
But that run came to an end at Brentford as he was given his first red card in his 351st Premier League appearance, although the decision has attracted plenty of debate.
His dismissal crucially means he will miss Sunday's Merseyside derby and also ruined David Moyes' record-breaking night as he took charge of his 593rd game as Everton boss - more than anyone else in the club's history.
The 4-0 loss was also the heaviest defeat Everton have had since Moyes returned to the club at the start of last year.
Tarkowski's dismissal proved a big talking point during and after the match, with opinions split on whether he should have gone. Even Moyes wasn't sure.
He told BBC Match of the Day: "My thoughts at the time, I didn't think it was but when I've looked at it again I think his foot high. Is there enough force for it to be a red card? Not sure about that."
Why did Tarkowski get sent off?
So what exactly happened?
Just 15 minutes after Keane Lewis-Potter scored his second deflected strike of the evening, Everton skipper Tarkowski thundered into a challenge on Brentford's Yehor Yarmoliuk.
He won the ball but also followed through with the challenge forcefully. Initially, referee Craig Pawson deemed a foul and a yellow card was enough.
But, after an intervention from the video assistant referee (VAR) and studying the replay, Pawson changed the yellow for a red.
The Premier League match centre said on X: "After VAR review, the referee overturned the original decision of yellow card for Tarkowski for the challenge on Yarmoliuk and issued a red card for serious foul play.
"VAR: 'Point of contact is on the shin. He's got speed and intensity. Studs are high.'
"REF: 'After review, Everton No.6 commits a challenge that endangers his opponent's safety, making contact with the studs onto the shin. Cancelling the yellow card - and a red card.'"
'Game's gone' or '100% red'? Experts are split
Referees are asked to take into account several considerations for what counts as serious foul play including the speed of the challenge, its intensity, force and what degree of control there was.
But, as always, there was plenty of debate about whether it was the correct decision.
BBC Sport's football issues correspondent Dale Johnson, said: "Really not sure about this as a VAR red card.
"Yes, Tarkowski absolutely ticks the boxes for speed and intensity and leading high with studs showing.
"But the question marks are that Tarkowski made only small contact and didn't have a straight leg when he did so.
"Maybe his reputation played a part? Remember, he wrongly escaped a VAR red card against Liverpool for a challenge, which was along the same lines. He won the ball and then followed through into Alexis Mac Allister. Thought that was a far stronger challenge."
BBC Radio 5 Live's - and former Blackburn Rovers striker - Chris Sutton, said on X: "Come on that's not a red… the game's gone."
Former Arsenal striker Alan Smith agreed the decision was harsh. He told Sky Sports: "Ten years ago we wouldn't have looked at it once and now we still [frame] it on the follow-through. I just can't see it.
"Only Tarkowski knows if he wanted to leave it high or if it was natural. The follow-through was just natural momentum.
"There's a bit of anger in there from Tarkowski and it's a little high but only he knows if he wanted to leave a little more on Yarmoliuk there."
Opinion was far from unanimous though, with both pundits in the Sky Sports studio adamant it was a clear red.
Former Liverpool centre-back Jamie Carragher said: "It's a red card. Tarkowski has got previous for tackles like that. He is a 90s defender, he tackles like that.
"He follows through with such force, it is excessive. You want to give him the benefit of the doubt but it's a red card."

Oscar Piastri: McLaren team boss Andrea Stella says he liked driver's fiery radio response to warnings to 'be careful' of Lando Norris
Oscar Piastri offered a fiery response to warnings from his McLaren team to "be careful" around his team-mate Lando Norris during the Las Vegas GP; watch the Qatar Grand Prix live on Sky Sports this weekend, with qualifying at 6pm on Saturday and the race at 4pm on Sunday
Monday 23 November 2026 18:53, UK
McLaren team principal Andrea Stella says he liked Oscar Piastri's fiery response to radio messages warning the Australian to "be careful" battling his team-mate Lando Norris during the Las Vegas Grand Prix.
Piastri started from 17th on the grid after taking an engine penalty but drove impressively - during an extraordinary race that featured 352 overtakes - to join the battle at the front in latter stages, closing in on a leading train of cars that featured Norris.
As Piastri chased George Russell for fourth with Norris just in front of the Mercedes, a radio exchange was played out on the television broadcast which featured him twice being told by his race engineer to "be careful" around his team-mate, to which he responded: "Stop telling me to ****ing be careful."

The McLaren pair ultimately benefitted from late errors by Russell and his Mercedes team-mate Antonelli to claim a double podium, with Norris second and Piastri third behind Red Bull's Max Verstappen.
Asked about Piastri's radio exchange after the race, Stella said: "I actually liked it. I like it. That's the character that you expect from a racer.
"It's not like the Michael Schumacher, the Fernando Alonso, the Kimi Raikkonen - that I worked with before - were any easier, and (they) were champions.
"That's the character you want to see. And that's also what you have to do from the pit wall. You need to make sure that the driver has a clear objective in his head.
"And you want to do it up until the point the driver makes you feel, 'I've got it. Don't go beyond.' That's exactly where you want to be from outside the cockpit.
"So, actually, well done to the pit wall and well done to Oscar in relation to this situation. That's exactly where we want to position the interaction between the team and the driver, and what we have learnt through some of the experiences we've gone through."
'You have to modulate and adapt a driver's racing spirit'
With Norris clearly outperforming Piastri this season, there have been relatively few challenges for McLaren in managing their drivers, which is in significant contrast to last season when Norris came out on top in a battle for the drivers' title that went down to the final race of the season.
The only major flashpoint of this season came when an aggressive attempt to pass Piastri from Norris on the final lap of the Sprint in Singapore resulted in contact that cost both drivers points, leading to criticism from Stella and an apology from the Brit.
Stella provided more detail on his approach to managing his drivers as he attempted to further explain why he liked Piastri's fierce radio response in Las Vegas.
"I'll have to up a little bit of IP (intellectual property) here, in terms of how you manage drivers, but let me be clear, because we avoid this matter to create any noise," Stella said to gathered reporters.
"If we go and we do a leisure go-karting together, our personalities will change slightly from the personality we have right now when we are enjoying sitting here. We will dig out the racing spirit, we will dig out something that is the reason why these guys do what they do, and all the sacrifices that they have gone through to be where they are.
"And that's where you have to come and help them, come and help them modulate, adapt. We want to use it. That's why I said I really liked Oscar's answer. That's the racer I want to see. But at the same time, it's a team effort in modulating it. We want to use just the right quantity of it that doesn't take us too far.
"And if you see Lando in Singapore, Lando certainly, you don't have to remind him of the team interest and that he's a team player. He's a phenomenal team player, yet his vision, his way of racing got a little too channelled, and in the final lap of the Sprint, he attacked Oscar in a way that led to a collision.
"And he was incredibly apologetic. And, if anything, he said like, 'guys, just don't assume that we do all the processing, because we are so busy just racing, keeping the car on track, and this year's car absorbs our bandwidth. So, just help us. Take it to the point where we can tell you, 'ok, that's enough. I've got it.''
"And that's exactly the point where we want to take it. The same message was given to both drivers, because that's a common learning. This is nothing to do with Oscar, this is just to do with dealing with drivers."
Stella's sympathy with all team bosses, not just Ferrari's Vasseur
McLaren also benefitted in Las Vegas from Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc colliding when they were also in contention for the leading positions.
Leclerc was given a 10-second penalty for causing the collision which spun Hamilton, and ultimately led to Ferrari failing to maximise the solid race pace they produced.
The incident was the latest in a series of clashes between the Ferrari drivers, with the previous one having cost the team a likely one-two in the Mexico City Grand Prix when Leclerc attempted to pass Hamilton for the lead on the opening lap.
Asked whether he had sympathy for his Ferrari counterpart Frederic Vasseur, Stella said: "When it comes to commenting on other teams, that's something I would not want to do. I can only say that it's a very difficult subject.
"Even last year, in which I would say we've been successful in managing two drivers in that sort of situation, fighting for their dream, which is the drivers' world championship, it's just been an incredible amount of work.
"Work that sometimes, I say, we paid in the fact that 2026 was affected by the effort that we needed to put into 2025.
"So, it's something that every team principal needs to deal with and it's probably one of the most difficult aspects to managing Formula 1, because it's the only one in which you can't simply say, 'let's go as a team.'
"Because the drivers, they compete for themselves. So, definitely sympathy, but for team principals in general, not only for Fred."

Apple confirms Ted Lasso will return for Season 5
The mustachioed coach will be back on the pitch dealing out folksy advice once again.
Ted Lasso, which everyone thought was ending with season three, has just been renewed for a fifth season. "Following its hit fourth season, Apple's global phenomenon Ted Lasso is officially returning back to the pitch for season five," Apple said in a press release, though it revealed no details about the show's next iteration.
The show wrapped up its storyline about the men's AFC Richmond Premier League squad (aka the Greyhounds) at the end of season three. Following the final episode of that season, called "So Long, Farewell," co-creator and lead actor Jason Sudeikis said "this is the end of the story we wanted to tell."
Thanks for believing.#TedLasso has been renewed for Season 5. pic.twitter.com/epfW8riG7b
— Apple TV (@AppleTV) November 23, 2026
Sounds pretty definitive! But then, the showrunners came up with the inspired idea for a fourth season: switching from the men's team to the Division 2 Lady Greyhounds. Though not quite hitting the critical heights of seasons one and two, it outperformed the Lasso's third run with an excellent 90 percent Rotten Tomatoes critical rating.
Season four ended with the Lady Greyhounds promoted to the women's Super League, ownership of the team settled and nice storyline wrap-ups for some of the main characters including Roy Kent, Keely, Coaches Lasso and Beard, Rebecca, and Alice Chilton. However, Apple didn't say if the show would stick with the Lady Greyhounds or shift its story elsewhere.
Love it or hate it, Ted Lasso is more than just a successful show for Apple TV. It was the platform's first bonafide hit, helping set a marker for future popular series like Severance, Silo, The Studio, Pluribus and Widow's Bay.

While exploring the eerie Silent Hill hotel easter egg, you can get your hands on some rare loot at the Marbelle Hotel. You will need the Marbelle Hotel safe code in GTA 6 to unlock the safe that’s in the downstairs office. So, check out the safe code and its location below to get cash and a collectible luxury watch. Don’t forget to look around for more collectibles while you’re here.
What Is the Haunted Marbelle Hotel Safe Code in GTA 6?
The Haunted Marbelle Hotel safe code in GTA 6 is 955214.
Unlike most four-digit safe codes in GTA 6 across Leonida, this safe’s keypad requires you to enter six digits.
You can enter 955214 immediately if you’re at the location. However, exploring upstairs will trigger the full Silent Hill easter egg and reveal the digits in-game, which is quite cool to experience.
Where to Find the Marbelle Hotel Safe Code in GTA 6?
Follow these steps to find the Marbelle Hotel safe code in GTA 6 and trigger the Silent Hill easter egg:
- Open your GTA 6 map and head to NW 8th Street in southern Crosstown, Vice City, right beside the highway and east of the Pawn and Gun shop.
- Walk down the left alley of Marbelle Hotel and enter the unlocked back door.
- Equip your flashlight using the GTA 6 gun-switching method in the binoculars slot since it’s dark inside.
- Climb the stairs to the top floor, and then you’ll spot a mannequin facing the wall.
- Turn right from the mannequin, and you’ll see a door that will open on its own, leading to a stairwell.
- Enter the stairwell and walk toward the roof door.
- As you climb, the lights cut out, whispers play, and glowing red graffiti appears on the wall with messages like “BURN TO DUST” as the room fills with fog.
- Look to your left, right next to the BURN TO DUST text, and you’ll see the numbers 955214 painted beside it.
- Wait for the lights to return and enter through the door to go to a foggy roof.
- There you will find an Old Notepad on the ground, so pick it up and read it.
- The second entry also lists the safe code 955214.
Now you’ve successfully found the Marbelle Hotel safe code in GTA 6. You’ll also see the entire Vice City plagued with dense fog, and you’ll only be able to clear it once you open the safe.
GTA 6 Marbelle Hotel (Silent Hill Hotel) Safe Location and Rewards
The abandoned Marbelle Hotel is easy to find once you know the right block in Vice City, and cracking its safe rewards you with cash and a rare GTA 6 collectible. Here’s the location of Marbelle Hotel and its loot.
Where to Find the Safe in the Haunted Marbelle Hotel
- Walk down the left alleyway of the Marbelle Hotel and enter through the unlocked back door.
- Walk past the staircase in the ground-floor office to find the grey safe tucked in the corner next to a red desk.
Marbelle Hotel Safe Loot and Valuables
Opening the Marbelle Hotel safe clears the Silent Hill fog that has taken over Vice City in GTA 6, and thus the safe rewards you with the following items:
- Crowex Ambassador “Breakfast” Watch: It is one of the 34 collectible Luxury Watches needed for 100% game completion.
- Cash: Two stacks totaling roughly $350
However, before you leave the hotel, climb the stairs to the second floor to find a wooden dresser on your left near the bed mannequin.
Go near it and you’ll find a bonus “Death of Swallow (Purple)” collectible card from The Legends of Ratface set.
You can keep it if you want and have Jason and Lucia wear it. But you can always flip it at a pawn shop to make money in GTA 6. So, wasn’t that easy?
Can you open the Marbelle Hotel Safe without a code in GTA 6?
No, you cannot open the Marbelle Hotel safe without the code in GTA 6. The keypad on the safe only accepts manual entry. With our code, you can skip the Silent Hill event and directly enter the code 955214 to open it.
Do you get a GTA 6 trophy for unlocking the Marbelle Hotel Safe?
Completing the Silent Hill event and unlocking the safe rewards you with the hidden trophy “The Truth Is Out There” in GTA 6. It will not unlock again if earned earlier from another paranormal encounter, like the Port Gellhorn UFO quest.

Jensen Huang is back, baby, and Wall Street is thrilled.
The chipmaker’s shares have surged more than 30 percent following the board’s announcement that it was reinstating Huang as president, CEO, and board member. The company’s valuation has soared by more than $1 trillion, which puts it on track to break Microsoft’s record for the greatest single-day gain in market value by hundreds of billions of dollars.
Huang departed the company he helped found on November 12 amid suspected asset-kissing and allegations of extramarital affairs with employees. Each report chipped away at the company’s value until nearly $2.2 trillion was erased over the past month.
Last week, board chair Harvey Jones said during the company’s earnings call that the board did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” WIRED also reported that Nvidia’s board had been alarmed by Huang’s “lack of candor” and “lying.”
And yet, despite all this, the board announced on Monday that it had brought Huang back—with some help from the US government. Semafor reported that, hours before Huang was reinstated, President Donald Trump dialed into the publicly traded company’s board meeting to argue for the ousted CEO’s return.
Many questions remain unanswered. What happens at the conclusion of the board-led investigation into Huang’s behavior? Multiple government agencies and lawmakers are reportedly investigating Huang; given the Trump administration’s aggressive support of the executive, what sort of accountability can anyone reasonably expect?
The turmoil has also raised red flags about what happens when so much of the market revolves around one person at one company. Nvidia has massive sway over the wider artificial intelligence ecosystem, due to its deals with and investments in other companies. Last week, the Nasdaq Composite dropped 10 percent, in part due to Nvidia’s struggles—the index’s biggest decline since March 2020.
On Monday morning, CNBC asked Trump if Nvidia’s influence on the stock market influenced his decision to push for Huang’s return. “Probably so, but the bigger impact was the long term,” Trump responded.
Trump, who has worked closely with Huang during his second administration, established himself as a vocal supporter of the CEO amid the recent chaos. Trump told The New York Times that he believed the board responded positively to his argument for Huang’s return because of the stock market dip, with the president suggesting that investors didn’t have much confidence in interim CEO Colette Kress.
“I just thought he should be running the company, and I didn’t know it was going to have this kind of an impact,” Trump told The New York Times. “I’ve never seen anything quite like it, actually. The stock is up.”
According to Trump, however, his decision wasn’t guided solely by the market.
“The bigger impact was, you know, he’s got other chips in his brain that nobody else knows about,” the president told CNBC. Sure!

An employee at the software company Figma said in a lawsuit filed Monday that she was sexually harassed by two of her colleagues at the company.
And after the incidents were reported, she says in the lawsuit that she was told to deal with them herself.
Her complaint, filed in federal court in New York, names Figma CEO Dylan Field as a defendant and accuses him of facilitating a company culture where harassment victims were encouraged to confront their harassers themselves.
"Figma's Confront-Your-Harasser Policy reflects the 'direct feedback' culture that CEO Dylan Field chose, publishes, and enforces," the complaint says. "And he has kept it in place to promote personal 'growth' for wrongdoers, at victims' expense."
Figma lists giving direct feedback as one of its company values, which is titled "Grow as you go."
In a statement, Figma said the claims were meritless.
"Figma does not tolerate discrimination or harassment," a spokesperson said.
"These claims have no merit, and we will present the facts in court," they added.
Field founded Figma in 2012 after receiving funding from PayPal founder Peter Thiel. Figma offers design products and services and competes directly with Adobe. Its stock price has slid steadily since its initial public offering last year.
The lawsuit seeks monetary compensation from Figma for emotional distress the employee said she endured. It says she took time off this year and was treated for PTSD symptoms and anxiety. The complaint also accuses Figma and Field of retaliation and discrimination.
Soon after the employee, who still works at Figma, joined the company in 2022 as a software engineer, she said her onboarding mentor asked her out on a date during a Zoom call, according to the lawsuit.
When she declined, she said the mentor told her to "think about it."
Then, after a holiday party during which she said the mentor "stalked her," she said in the lawsuit that she reported his behavior to one of her managers, who allegedly dismissed her complaint as harmless flirting, adding that he had met his wife at work too.
The employee also sought to have her alleged harasser kept off her project, and Figma's human resources told her to confront her harasser herself, the lawsuit said.
"She already had confronted him — having rejected his advances several times," the complaint says.
In 2024, the employee said in the lawsuit that she transferred to another team at Figma, where a year later her new manager allegedly made a crass joke about the employee and her wife having sex.
Another employee recognized that the joke made the plaintiff uncomfortable and reported it to Figma's HR department. Even though the employee, the target of the joke, hadn't made the complaint, a member of Figma's HR department told her to confront the manager herself, the lawsuit claims.
The HR department ultimately closed the investigation into the new manager after the superior claimed to have used the word "SEV" — a cybersecurity severity ranking — rather than "sex," the lawsuit says.
The plaintiff is being represented by New York employment law firm Seppinni Law.
"Our client hopes with today's lawsuit that Figma will start taking women at the company, and especially their sexual harassment complaints, more seriously," Shane Seppinni, the firm's founder, told Business Insider.

Sooryavanshi, 15, breaks sixes record by scoring 204 off 53 balls
- Published
India's 15-year-old batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hit the most sixes ever recorded in a senior men's innings in blazing 204 from 53 balls for India A against the United Arab Emirates.
While almost halving the record for the fastest double-century in List A cricket, Sooryavanshi hit 28 sixes and seven fours in the Asia Cup Rising Stars competition - easily breaking Chad Bowes' previous record of 103 balls from 2024.
The teenage opener also broke the record for the fastest century and 150, the latter of which he already held, before being caught at long-off with his side five runs from victory.
India A ultimately passed their target of 250, played against a UAE side that featured a number of internationals but was not their current first-choice side, in 14.2 overs in Doha.
Sooryavanshi now holds the following records in List A cricket, the categorisation given to senior one-day matches:
- Fastest fifty: 11 balls v Sri Lanka A, 21 June (previously Kaushalya Weeraratne, 12 balls, 1 November 2005)
- Fastest hundred: 28 balls, today (previously Jake Fraser-McGurk, 29 balls, 8 October 2023)
- Fastest 150: 40 balls, today (previously himself, 59 balls, 24 December 2025)
- Fastest 200: 52 balls, today (previously Chad Bowes, 103 balls, 22 October 2024)
The previous record for the most sixes in senior matches was 26, struck by Tanmay Agarwal in an innings of 366 for Hyderabad against Arunachal Pradesh in India's first-class Ranji Trophy competition in January 2024.
The record in List A cricket was 23 sixes, struck by D'Arcy Short for Queensland in his 257 against Tasmania on 28 September 2018.
Sooryavanshi has rapidly become a sensation in T20 cricket since making his debut in the Indian Premier League in 2025 at the age of 14.
He has hit two hundreds and six fifties in his first two seasons in the competition and has earned 10 caps for India in the shortest format since making his debut against England in July.
The left-hander, who was batting in only his 16th List A innings in Doha and made his second century in the format, is yet to play for India in 50-over cricket.
He put on partnerships of 68 with opening partner Abhishek Sharma, who scored 12, 40 with Prabhsimran Singh, who added just three, and 137 with Rinku Singh, who scored an unbeaten 27.
The India A side, which featured a number of internationals, restricted the UAE to 249-8 in 50 overs, external after their opposition had chosen to bat and swiftly reached 254-3 to win by seven wickets and guarantee their place in the semi-finals.
The Rising Stars competition features A sides from India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and Afghanistan alongside squads from the UAE, Nepal and Hong Kong.
India A, who now top Group B, beat Nepal and lost to Pakistan A in their previous two matches in the competition, with Sooryavanshi making scores of 26 and 11.
Pakistan A will retake the top spot if they beat Nepal on Tuesday, with semi-finals on Thursday and Friday to follow before Sunday's final.

India, China conclude 10-day talks to ease Arunachal LAC tensions before winter
India and China concluded 10 days of military talks on managing tensions along the Arunachal LAC. The discussions focused on preventing confrontations and maintaining communication before harsh winter conditions set in.
India and China have concluded a second round of Corps Commander-level talks aimed at easing tensions along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh, with both sides discussing ways to prevent local confrontations from escalating into larger military standoffs ahead of winter.
The discussions, which began on November 8 and continued for nearly 10 days with a brief break in between, were described as cordial, according to defence sources. The Indian delegation was led by Lieutenant General Girish Kalia, General Officer Commanding of the Army's III Corps, also known as the Spear Corps. His Chinese counterpart and other military officers participated in the discussions. An official from the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) was also present.
The talks covered a broad range of issues concerning troop engagement practices along the frontier, including the need to maintain communication channels and prevent local friction between personnel deployed on either side of the LAC from escalating.
The latest engagement comes at a critical time, with winter approaching in the eastern sector. Severe weather conditions, snowfall and difficult terrain can significantly hamper troop movement, logistics and the maintenance of forward deployments along the frontier.
SECOND ROUND FOLLOWS SEPTEMBER MEETING
The latest discussions follow the first Senior Highest Military Commander-Level Flag Meeting in the eastern sector, held on September 6 at Wacha on the Indian side in Arunachal Pradesh and on September 7 at Damai on the Chinese side.
The meeting marked the extension of the senior military commander-level engagement mechanism to the eastern sector. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal had confirmed the September meetings, saying they were held pursuant to understandings reached between the Special Representatives of India and China in August 2025 and August 2026, followed by discussions under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC) on India-China Border Affairs in May and August 2026.
The September engagement came amid reports of tensions in the Taksing area of Arunachal Pradesh's Upper Subansiri district, where Indian and Chinese troops had reportedly come face to face.
The Indian delegation at the September meeting was also led by Lieutenant General Girish Kalia. A similar senior military commander-level engagement mechanism already exists in the western sector.
WINTER, TROOP DEPLOYMENT ADD TO SIGNIFICANCE
The latest round assumes significance as both countries continue to maintain substantial troop deployments along the eastern frontier. Establishing clear engagement practices and maintaining communication between military commanders are important to prevent misunderstandings or local confrontations from escalating.
The discussions also come amid broader efforts by New Delhi and Beijing to stabilise bilateral relations. During Prime Minister Narendra Modi's meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit in New Delhi on September 12, both leaders emphasised that peace and tranquillity in border areas remained essential for the continued development of bilateral ties.
The Prime Minister also stressed the need for both sides to adhere to existing agreements and understandings on border-related issues.
Separately, Union Home Minister Amit Shah reviewed border security and strategic infrastructure in Arunachal Pradesh during a high-level meeting in Itanagar on November 21. The government said the review focused on strengthening security coordination and expanding road connectivity, border outposts, helipads and telecommunications facilities in areas along the China border.
The latest military discussions are part of continued efforts to maintain peace and stability along the LAC. However, details of any specific agreement or outcome from the November talks have not been officially made public.

Following the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), the Special Summary Revision (SSR) is now underway in Uttar Pradesh, with the stated objective of preparing an error-free electoral roll. An analysis of Form 6 applications by Alt News, however, reveals a sharp and unprecedented surge in applications for inclusion in the electoral roll, with daily submissions rising from a few thousand in early November to over four lakh by November 22.
The SSR process began with the publication of the draft electoral rolls on November 17. About two weeks earlier, on October 30, Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath had said at a BJP state working committee meeting in Lucknow that the names of around 1.27 crore Hindu voters were missing from the electoral rolls. He urged party workers to launch a systematic campaign to ensure their inclusion.
Again, on November 22, The Indian Express reported that Uttar Pradesh BJP had instructed its workers to focus on Form 6 additions in the SSR is to ensure inclusion of names of individuals eligible to be voters but left out during the SIR for some reason.
Tracking Form 6 application data from the SSR process, Alt News found that between November 1 and 16, an average of around 10,000 applications were submitted daily across the state. The numbers began rising sharply from November 17, the day the draft rolls were published, and accelerated dramatically over the following five days. On November 22 alone, around 4.16 lakh applications were submitted.
What Alt News Found
An analysis of Form 6 application data from Uttar Pradesh shows that around 2,000 applications were filed across the state on November 1. The numbers began rising the following day, with around 10,000 applications submitted on November 2. A similar number were filed on November 3 and 4, followed by 9,000 on November 5.
The state recorded around 12,000 applications each on November 6 and 7, before the figure dropped to 4,000 on November 8. Around 9,000 applications were submitted on November 9.
On November 10, 11 and 12, the daily figures stood at 15,000, 16,000 and 15,000, respectively. Applications declined to around 11,000 each on November 13 and 14, and further to 9,000 on both November 15 and 16.
The pace of submissions changed significantly on November 17, when the SSR process began and the draft electoral roll was published. Around 31,000 Form-6 applications were filed across Uttar Pradesh that day. The numbers climbed further over the next two days, with 46,000 applications on November 18 and 68,000 on November 19. On November 20, the figure stood at around 60,851.
The surge became even more pronounced from November 21, when around 2.31 lakh Form-6 applications were submitted. The following day, November 22, the figure more than doubled to approximately 4.16 lakh.
Who Are Filing these Applications?
Alt News’s analysis found that some of the new applicants had been deleted from the electoral rolls during the SIR.
To identify such applicants, the Alt News team matched new Form 6 applicants against the 2.89 crore names deleted during the SIR under the categories of absent, shifted, dead or duplicate.
Of the approximately 10.4 lakh applications examined between October 29 and November 22, Alt News found around 45,000 applicants whose names had been deleted during the SIR and who were now applying for inclusion in the electoral roll of the same assembly constituency. These applicants accounted for around 4.3% of all the applications examined.
Put another way, the 45,000 applicants represent approximately 1.6 in every 1,000 people whose names were deleted during the SIR (45,000 out of 2.89 crore). Most of these applicants had previously been marked as absent or shifted before their names were deleted.
A Closer Look at Form 6 Applications
A closer examination of the Form 6 applications reveals several serious anomalies, like instances of multiple applications carrying identical applicant details.
In Siwalkhas assembly constituency in Meerut district, for instance, 44 applications were submitted from the same address: “Gotka, Gotka, Gotka, Gotka, 250344, Sardhana.” All 44 applications were filed on November 5 and 6.
Alt News also identified 6,969 repeat Form-6 applications submitted between November 20 and 22.
These repeat applications were found within the same assembly constituency and carried identical applicant names and father’s or husband’s names.
For instance, in Bindki constituency in Fatehpur district, an applicant named Himanshu submitted five Form 6 applications. Four were filed on November 21 and another on November 22. All five applications carry the same applicant name, his father’s name, Baburam, and the same address.
The application serial numbers also show that three of these applications were submitted consecutively.
In another instance, Alt News identified an applicant named Aadhya Seth who submitted six Form 6 applications over three days, between November 20 and 22. In all six applications, the applicant’s name, father’s name and address are identical.
To identify similar instances, we matched applicants by name and their father’s or husband’s name within each constituency for the period October 29 to November 22. The exercise identified 10,773 individuals whose names appeared more than once, accounting for 11,684 additional applications.
According to Alt News’s analysis, approximately one in every 90 Form 6 applications was a repeat submission. The analysis also identified 427 individuals who had submitted applications in two different assembly constituencies.
The data shows that most repeat applications were filed on the same day, often in immediate succession.
A closer analysis also reveals that repeat applications increased alongside the overall surge in Form 6 submissions. On November 17, 18 and 19, the number of repeat applications stood at 340, 458 and 699, respectively. Before this, the daily figure had rarely crossed 400, reaching around that mark only on November 10 and 15.
On November 22 alone, however, 4,325 repeat applications were submitted. This means approximately one in every 100 Form 6 applications filed that day was a repeat submission.
Making Sense of the Surge
The overall volume of applications saw a sharp increase ever since the SSR draft role had been published. Between October 29 and November 22, a total of 10,56,778 Form 6 applications were submitted across Uttar Pradesh. Of these, 1,65,289 were filed between November 1 and 16, while 4,37,235 were submitted in just five days, between November 17 and 21.
On November 22 alone, the number stood at 4,16,380. According to data compiled by the Alt News team, more Form-6 applications were submitted on November 22 than during the first 20 days of November combined.
According to the figures available from November 20 to November 22, Kheri district (33,836) saw the most number of Form 6 applications. Other districts such as Ghaziabad (25,438), Agra (24,715), Barabanki (21,652), Prayagraj (21,433), Azamgarh (20,642), Bareily (20,625), Lucknow (20,369), Unnao (16,376) and Bulandshahr (16,217) also saw significant number of applications.
Interestingly, Ghaziabad and Bulandshahr showed zero entry on November 20. So all the applications for these two districts are from November 21 and November 22.
Ghaziabad district recorded the highest number of Form 6 applications so far on November 22, with 39,828 submissions. Other districts with substantial numbers of applications include Agra (39,091), Lucknow (32,324), Kheri (27,904), Prayagraj (19,764) , Azamgarh (19,135) , Fatehpur (18,253), Bulandshahr (18,120), Barabanki (15,782), Bareily (15,096) and Gorakhpur (12,474).
A similar trend was observed in constituencies such as Loni, Ghaziabad, Lakhimpur, Etmadpur, Zaidpur, Bangermau, Dadri, Chakia and Barabanki.
Across the state, an assembly constituency typically recorded an average of around 17 Form 6 applications between November 1 and 16. However, the average rose sharply to 496 applications on November 21 and further to 966 on November 22.
Amid this surge, however, some pockets of western Uttar Pradesh recorded no substantial number of Form 6 applications. For instance, in Bijnor district, eight constituencies recorded no Form 6 applications, according to the compiled Form 9 lists on November 20 and 21. In Muzaffarnagar, six constituencies recorded a similar trend on November 20 and 21, while 22 constituencies did so on November 22.
Similar patterns were observed in pockets of Saharanpur, Moradabad, Meerut, Rampur, Bulandshahr and Shamli, among other districts.
The Back Story
On April 10, the final SIR roll for Uttar Pradesh was published. The total voters in the state plummeted from 15.44 crores to 13.39 crores in the process.
In December 2025, Yogi Adityanath warned that nearly 4 crore eligible voters could be missing during the SIR, claiming that 85-90% of them could be BJP supporters. Following the publication of the draft electoral roll on January 6, which reportedly recorded around 2.89 crore deletions, the BJP expressed concern, particularly over urban constituencies, and mobilised workers to help voters re-enroll.
In January 2026, a Newslaundry report said that the BJP was worried that large-scale deletions in urban constituencies could affect its electoral prospects. In 50 constituencies, more than one lakh voters had reportedly been deleted, 47 of which the BJP had won in 2022. The final roll, published on April 10, 2026, contained approximately 13.39 crore electors, down from around 15.44 crore before the SIR, with several BJP minister held constituencies reportedly recording substantial deletions.
On October 30, Adityanath claimed that 1.27 crore Hindu voters were missing, citing discrepancies involving panchayat electoral rolls, welfare beneficiaries and young voters. He mentioned 66 lakh names allegedly present on panchayat rolls but absent from Assembly rolls, 55 lakh welfare beneficiaries and approximately 4.5 lakh young voters.
On November 14, the BJP reportedly set targets of restoring 10,000–25,000 voters per assembly constituency, with party leaders estimating that 40–80 lakh voters could be re-enrolled. Following the publication of the SSR draft roll on November 17, the party planned to launch a booth-level voter addition campaign from November 20.

Why Potts swapped West Ham for Club Brugge after 16 years
- Published
When Liverpool visit Club Brugge on Wednesday they are likely to come up against English midfielder Freddie Potts.
The 23-year-old ended a 16-year association with West Ham in the summer to join the Belgian champions for an undisclosed fee.
And he has started every game, bar one missed through suspension, in all competitions.
After losing to Aston Villa in the Champions League, they have defeated Inter Milan, Lens and PSV.
"It really is a dream because you hear the music and then you see your family in the stands and you remember all the times that you watched Champions League on TV," Potts told BBC Radio 5 Live's Euro Leagues Show.
"You think of all the memories that you make watching it and to be playing in it now is something that every kid dreams of."
Potts' whole life had been based around West Ham. He had been with the club since the age of six and his father Steve, who made 506 appearances for the Hammers, is a first-team coach.
Potts Jr played 28 times for West Ham, with 25 of them coming last season as they were relegated from the Premier League.
He also had loan spells with Wycombe in League One and Portsmouth in the Championship.
"In pre-season my minutes with West Ham were limited, they weren't as much as I wanted and then I spoke with my agent and said 'let's explore options because this season I'm 22, turning 23'," Potts said.
"It's a massive part of my career and I wanted to play. The opportunity of Club Brugge came along with Champions League football, the best club in Belgium and it was an opportunity I couldn't really turn down with how my minutes were going down with West Ham.
"I grew up in the area, going to the stadium watching the games. It was always going to be a tough decision but it was something that I had to do for my career.
"It was an emotional decision because it had to be made quite quickly. It's been the right decision for me and so far I'm enjoying it, I'm loving life here."
Club Brugge won the Belgian title last season and are second, just one point behind leaders Union Saint-Gilloise this campaign.
"It's a physical league," said Potts. "My running and physical stats have been higher than they've ever been. It's a demanding league in that way.
"Club Brugge demands a lot, from winning the ball back and going man for man in the press. And your responsibility off the ball is something that you have to take really seriously."
Potts says he has not started to learn French or Flemish and that team talks are done in English, with the side managed by Croat Ivan Leko.
And he revealed he has a lifelong history with the city.
"The whole move itself is funny because we used to visit Brugge when I was a kid," he said.
"We used to come around Christmas, so my family all know the city. And now I'm here they come out as much as they can.
"It's a great city with a lot of culture. It's brilliant. You won't find many places like it."
Next up for the side is the visit of Liverpool this week - with both clubs on nine points after four games.
The Reds are eighth and Club Brugge are ninth in the table.
"Everyone knows Liverpool as a club, the size and the Premier League teams," said Potts, who started for West Ham at home to the Reds last season.
"It's going to be a big game. We're level on points in the Champions League and we've put big performances in this competition and we're hoping that we're going to do the same."

Nato chief vows defence against space threat after Russian nuclear satellite reports
- Published
Nato chief Mark Rutte has said the alliance will defend against any threats in space after reports that Russia was preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite.
Intelligence reports about a possible launch in the next 60 days had been shared among Nato countries this month, according to German media outlets. It was not clear which country had authored the reports.
Asked about the reports, Rutte said: "We will always make sure we defend every inch of Nato territory, and that includes making sure we are safe when it comes to the space element."
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he hadn't seen the latest reports but dismissed reports citing "unknown sources" as "hardly worth taking seriously".
The Russian embassy in Berlin told German media it rejected what it called "unfounded allegations" and said the reports were part of a "propaganda campaign".
Rutte told the press conference in Berlin that Nato had a variety of response options.
"When it comes to the military domain, we will always make assessments of our deterrence and defence and make updates where necessary," he said.
Citing anonymous German military and intelligence sources, the reports by broadcasters NDR and WDR, and newspaper Sueddeutsche Zeitung, said the Russian satellite was dubbed "Sputnik-S" and was equipped with a nuclear warhead. It could be used to disrupt or destroy other satellites, including important communication and observation satellites.
Standing alongside Rutte, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz did not confirm or deny the reports of Russia's plans, but said they "reveal the level of escalation Russia is evidently prepared to pursue".
"Reports that Russia is planning to introduce nuclear weaponry into space are not new, yet they remain no less shocking," he said.
A German government spokesman earlier also did not confirm or deny the reports, but said it was taking the reports "very seriously", AFP reported. The spokesman, however, warned against causing "excessive nervousness regarding hypothetical dangers".
Josef Aschbacher, the head of the European Space Agency, said having nuclear weapons in space was "the ultimate nightmare scenario", German paper Handelsblatt reported.
Russia is a signatory to the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, which bans weapons of mass destruction from orbit. Other countries, including the US and China, have deployed or plan to deploy other weapons in space, exploring other capabilities outside of the treaty, such as targeting rivals' satellites - which are key for military communications, surveillance and navigation.
In 2024 the US claimed Russia was developing a "space-based" anti-satellite weapon armed with a nuclear warhead. Russia denied the accusation.
"Our position is clear and transparent. We have always been categorically against the deployment of nuclear weapons in space and we are still against it," President Vladimir Putin said at the time.
In September the US Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink said the US had "on-orbit, space-control weapons" circling the planet, but did not provide specifics. In response to the announcement, the Kremlin's Peskov told Russian media that space "must be free of any weapon".

'I'm not a hero,' says Arizona man who found lost toddler alone in the desert
Police, dogs and drones scoured area for 2-year-old to no avail. Then Jay Stewart found her in a bush
Jay Stewart has a lot of precious memories, but he says nothing compares to the moment he found two-year-old Vella Campillo alone in the cold, dark Arizona desert, wearing nothing but a diaper.
Police are hailing Stewart as a hero after he found the missing toddler who wandered away from her backyard last week, sparking a massive search-and-rescue operation in the rural community of Eloy, Ariz.
"I am so grateful to have experienced that life event, because there's no other feeling like it in the world," Stewart told As It Happens host Nil Köksal.  
"That's No. 1 in my life, the most emotional moment I've ever had."
Vella was unharmed and has been safely reunited with her parents, police said.
Vella was reported missing around 6 p.m., local time, on Nov. 17, according to the Pinal County Sheriff's Office.
Her parents, Joseph Campillo and Deanna Fritz, told Fox News affiliate KSAZ that she'd been playing in the backyard with her siblings under the care of another family member when she wandered off.
Officials from several police and fire departments spent hours scouring the area along with dozens of volunteers, two helicopters, K-9 units and heat-detecting drones, all to no avail.
Then, just after midnight, Stewart called Vella's name and saw her pop out of a tiny patch of plants in the desert.
"I spun around, and she jumped back down into this little bush … the size of, like, four dinner plates put together," he said. "She almost looked like she was swimming. Her little arms were moving around like she was treading water."
Pitch black and freezing cold
Stewart and his wife had been looking for Vella ever since the emergency alert hit their phones notifying people of a missing child in their area.
They spent two hours searching along the side of the road, he says, before heading home to check the news and bundle up in warmer clothes as the sun went down and the cold set in.
"The desert is kind of like being in a mine. It could be pitch black where you can't see anything. And that's what it was like," he said.
On their second try, they drove into the desert behind Vella's home on their ATV.
"I've lived out there 20 years and I fly over it all the time in our helicopter. So I know it like the back of my hand," he said. "It's my backyard."
Pinal County Sheriff Ross Teeple, right, awarded Stewart a plaque and a badge the day after he found a missing toddler near Eloy, Ariz. (Pinal County Sheriff’s Office)
Stewart says he'd separated from his wife as he wandered about a mile down a ditch calling Vella's name. He heard a yell, then saw her pop up and back down again.
He reached down, plucked her into his arms, unzipped his jacket and tucked her inside.
"She whimpered for about 15 seconds when I picked her up, and then once I snuggled her to me and got her, she seemed pretty happy," he said. "She warmed up pretty quick."
Stewart says she didn't make a peep until he dropped his phone while talking to a 911 dispatcher.
"And she went, 'Phone!' I started laughing. And I'm like, 'Yeah, baby, phone!' " he said. "It chokes me up. I can hear that little voice."

Within 10 minutes, he says, police and other searchers were on the scene.
Body cam footage released by the Pinal County Sheriff's Office shows Stewart holding the toddler on his hip. By that point, she was wrapped in a blanket provided by another searcher and chattering away happily in baby talk.
When the officer took Vella to check her over, the little girl clutched onto Stewart.
"She wouldn't let go of me," he said.
'The very best of our community'
At a news conference on Nov. 18, Sheriff Ross Teeple awarded Stewart a plaque and a badge for his community service.
"Your selflessness and willingness to get involved amplify the very best of our community," Teeple said. "Your actions remind us that every citizen has the power to make a meaningful difference and that sometimes, the greatest acts of service come from simply choosing to help."
But Stewart says he was just one of dozens of volunteers who showed up for Vella, and he happened to get lucky.
"I'm not a hero. I'm a searcher, just like everyone else was," he said.
He called the rescue the most emotional moment of his life, followed by the birth of his children and the day he married his wife.
"The reason I put it ahead of my kids is because I knew where my kids were. They weren't lost. I was holding them," he said. "But to find something that's lost like that, helpless and lost? I can only imagine what the parents were going through."
