The copypasta was a version of a message that previously circulated before the 2024 U.S. presidential election, warning people in Gwinnett County, Georgia, against possible attacks on Black voters. At the time, the Gwinnett County Sheriff's Office said on social media the warning was a hoax.
After the 2026 U.S. midterm elections, many social media users shared the same piece of text — something known as a copypasta — warning about the threat of an attack from white supremacists and the Ku Klux Klan on Black people in the U.S (archived)
The message read:
I just received this from a friend who works in the Sheriff's office!! 
Be on Alert... Last night, a deputy told a family that local White Supremacists/ KKK members originating out of Lexington, NC, are planning to attack from now until the Inauguration.
They are plotting against Blacks, especially black women because in their eyes, we are easy targets! Please be vigilant!
Try not to do anything alone, especially after dark! This is not a hoax or a rumor! The deputy showed paperwork that the police department has. In their words..."They're taking their country back!"
It's really scary, and please take what I'm telling you SERIOUSLY!
We have to continue to live, but JUST BE CAREFUL and watch your surroundings!
This is happening everywhere. Stay safe!"
Take care of yourself & please share!!! "
A friend of mine sent this to me. I'd rather be safe than sorry. 
The people relaying the message on Facebook appeared to live in Alabama, Virginia, Georgia or Michigan. None specified an exact location for the supposed attacks.
One version of the introduction to the message said it came from a "valid source," adding "Magga is upset," presumable referring to U.S. President Donald Trump's movement, Make America Great Again, which lost significant ground to Democrats in the 2026 elections (archived):
As in many instances of copypasta and urban legends, those who shared the message claimed to have received it from close relations — a tried-and-true way of giving a claim the appearance of credibility. Our reporting, however, indicates that there is no truth in it.
In reality, versions of this message have been circulating since at least 2024 (archived), before the day of the presidential election. A version we checked then, which said the warning came from the sheriff's office in Gwinnett County, Georgia, read, in part:
Fwd:
Hey ladies, I just received this from a friend who works in the Gwinnett County Sheriff's office!!!
Be on Alert… Last night, a deputy told a family that local White Supremacists/ KKK members originating out of Lexington, NC, are planning to attack from now until the Inauguration.
They are plotting against Blacks, especially black women because in their eyes, we are easy targets! Please be vigilant! Try not to do anything alone, especially after dark! This is not a hoax or a rumor! The deputy showed paperwork that the police department has. In their words…They're taking their country back!"
It's really scary, and please take what I'm telling you SERIOUSLY! We have to continue to live, but just be careful and watch your surroundings!
This is happening everywhere. Stay safe!"
Take care of yourself.
Watch and make people aware of anything abnormal!!!
Snopes reported on this message at the time.
As part of our research then, Snopes contacted the Gwinnett County's Sheriff's Office, which told us it was aware of such a message circulating. The office directed us to its social media posts addressing it. The post on its Facebook page indicated that while it had not received any information about this specific threat, it would remain attentive to any concerning activity designed to derail the voting process. It also suggested that the reason some people are spreading this rumor might be to discourage voters — especially Black women — from going to polling stations to cast their ballots (archived):
(Facebook/Gwinnett County Sheriff's Office)
The Gwinnett County Sheriff's Office has been made aware of a circulating text thread suggesting potential attacks on African American women "from now through the inauguration." We have not received any information indicating threats to any group(s) on or after election day.
Hateful discourse such as this aims to instill fear in the community and disrupt us from exercising our constitutional rights. The Gwinnett County Sheriff's Office remains dedicated to protecting all citizens and we will continue to monitor and respond accordingly to all suspicious and threatening behavior.
We will continue collaborating with local, state, and federal authorities to stay current on any potential threats surrounding the general election. Please immediately report any information regarding threats or suspicious behavior to your local law enforcement agency or call the Tip Line at 770.619.6655.
The lack of specificity of the 2026 version of this message made it more likely to spread across the country. However nothing indicated a heightened level of threat. We searched Google, DuckDuckGo and Yahoo for reports of such a threat. No such story appeared in any reputable news outlet as of this writing, indicating there was no basis to believe the posts' claims.
For further reading, Snopes has covered several instances of copypastas, including one that made false and misleading claims about registered voter numbers and fraud in Wisconsin and Texas in November 2026.

84 days, four titles, one historic feat - Alcaraz's remarkable return
- Published
The men's tennis season ended as it began, with a beaming Carlos Alcaraz holding aloft one of the sport's biggest trophies.
In January, he won the Australian Open to complete the career Grand Slam. Ten months later, he stood as the victor in Turin, having ended his wait for a first ATP Finals title.
Watching Alcaraz over recent weeks, it would be easy to forget that for a four-month period this year, the 23-year-old barely picked up a racquet.
He missed the majority of the clay and all of the grass-court season with a wrist injury, but he has made a remarkable return, culminating in a dismantling of world number one Alexander Zverev on Sunday.
It is 84 days since Alcaraz made his comeback at the US Open, where his lack of match fitness understandably showed. He came through the early rounds but lost a five-set quarter-final epic against Ben Shelton.
Since then, the Spaniard has won 21 of his 22 matches - including each of the past 14 - and captured titles at four of the five tournaments he has contested.
He continues to make history, too, becoming the youngest man to win all four Slams and the season-ending Finals.
This was the third straight tournament he has won, following victories at the Vienna Open and Paris Masters earlier in November, and he has now won his past nine matches against fellow top-10 players.
The former world number one, currently ranked third behind Zverev and Jannik Sinner, continues to make up for lost time as he seeks to quickly reassert himself at the top of the sport.
"I think everybody feels he's the number one," Alcaraz said, stressing each player in the game has to treat themselves that way.
"Me, Sascha [Zverev], Jannik [Sinner], [Ben] Shelton. Having that confidence in yourself is really important.
"But right now the number one is Sascha. He really deserves it."
- Alcaraz outplays Zverev for first ATP Finals triumph 
  - Published11 hours ago
Crowd-pleasing variety, devastating power and astonishing athleticism did not take long to return to Alcaraz's game.
Even with a heavily strapped left leg after injuring his hamstring on Wednesday, he could not be stopped by the world's top players in Turin.
That included Zverev, who this year rose to the top of the rankings for the first time after claiming his first two major titles and recording a tour-leading 69 match wins.
Alcaraz, already a seven-time Slam winner, feels his own growth in the mental side of the sport has taken him to a different level in recent months.
He has specifically pointed to the new sense of perspective he gained from his time away from tennis in inspiring his scintillating year-end form.
"The injury made me realise what's really important," Alcaraz said.
"It's not winning. It's just about playing tennis. I realised that it is a gift every time that I can step on the court and compete healthy.
"When you realise that, everything comes easier.
"I don't feel stressed most of the time. I think right now I'm more mature, or I feel that, on a tennis court, I'm facing the problems and difficult moments in a different way."
Alcaraz threw himself to the ground after ending his wait to win the season-ending tournament before racing into the stands to celebrate with his team and family.
It marked the 30th title of his career, drawing him level with rival Sinner and behind only men's record 24-time major winner Novak Djokovic (102) among active ATP players.
More could soon be around the corner - should he manage to stay injury-free.
Victory in Paris has left him two titles away from emulating Sinner and Djokovic by completing the career 'Golden Masters' - winning all nine Masters 1,000 events, the level of tournament below the Slams.
Should he achieve that next season in Canada and Shanghai, it would leave him only an Olympic singles gold away from completing the sport.
His main obstacle to achieving such dominance still appears to be Sinner, given Alcaraz's positive head-to-head against Zverev.
Italian Sinner has been absent with a knee issue since Wimbledon but is aiming to return, external at the Australian Open, where Alcaraz will defend his title in January.
"In today's final, I needed to put the three Cs - cabeza, corazon, cojones - that my grandpa always tells me I have to give every time I step on the court," Alcaraz said.
"The three Cs in English is head, heart and balls. Today, that was what it was about.
"Lifting this trophy is something I have been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me."

The Department of Health and Family Welfare on Thursday launched the Karnataka State Action Plan for Containment of Antimicrobial Resistance (KSAPCAR) during a State-level workshop on antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in Bengaluru.
The action plan was formally unveiled by Rajini M, Director, Health and Family Welfare Services, to focus on strengthening antimicrobial stewardship, surveillance, infection prevention and control, and One Health collaboration to address the growing threat of AMR, said a release.
The workshop brought together Deputy Directors of Health and Family Welfare Services, District Surveillance Officers, District Epidemiologists, District Microbiologists, medical college faculty, programme officers, and public health professionals from across the State.
In her inaugural address, Dr. Rajini highlighted AMR as a major public health challenge and emphasised the need for rational antimicrobial use, stronger laboratory and surveillance systems, robust infection prevention practices, and coordinated action across human, animal, and environmental health sectors.
“The launch of KSAPCAR marks a significant step toward a coordinated, evidence-based response to antimicrobial resistance and is expected to accelerate implementation of AMR containment measures across Karnataka, helping preserve the effectiveness of life-saving antimicrobials for future generations,” the release added.

South Korea on Friday reported its first case of cholera in 10 years, with health authorities urging people to take precautionary measures, use only safe water and wash their food properly.
The Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency said health workers confirmed cholera from test samples of a person who had visited a hospital emergency room in the southeastern port city of Changwon earlier this month, showing symptoms of vomiting and diarrhea.
The agency said the unidentified person, who recovered and was discharged on Tuesday, had not travelled overseas in the past two months. It said health workers were trying to trace the source of infection and the people the person had been in contact with.
It was the country's first case of cholera since 2016, when authorities identified three cases suspected to be caused by contaminated seafood. At least 162 people got sick in a larger outbreak in 2001.
The agency issued guidance urging people to stick to safe water and cooked food and to wash and peel fruits and vegetables. It also urged medical facilities to promptly test and report suspected cases.

In November, a video (archived) circulated that social media users claimed authentically shows a group of Muslims calling themselves "Soldiers of Allah" and demanding Shariah be put in place in Manchester, England.
According to the Council on Foreign Relations, a U.S. foreign policy think tank, Shariah is "the divine counsel that Muslims follow to live moral lives and grow close to God." Interpretations of Shariah, the principles of which stem from the Quran and hadith, the latter of which are sayings attributed to the Prophet Muhammad, form the basis of Islamic law.
The video in question shows people gathered on Wilmslow Road in Rusholme, south of Manchester, a stretch of road that is also known as the "Curry Mile" for its large number of restaurants specializing in South Asian and Middle Eastern food. The footage shows large groups of people, who appeared to be majority male, chanting and beating their chests.
One Instagram user who shared the video wrote:
A large group of military-age men took to the streets in a Manchester suburb calling themselves soldiers of Allah and demanding sharia law be put in place because they now form the majority in the neighborhood. The march was open and organized, not a quiet gathering. When a neighborhood shifts demographically and then the new majority starts openly calling for a different legal system, the question is how far that demand is expected to go. Local officials and residents are left deciding whether this is just free expression or the start of parallel rules. Do you think this is being handled the right way in the UK?
The footage also circulated on Facebook (archived). Snopes readers searched our site for information about the clips.
The video appears authentic, meaning it shows an event that actually happened and wasn't created used artificial intelligence. However, people who shared in it November miscaptioned the footage.
It doesn't show Muslims calling themselves "Soldiers of Allah" or calling for Shariah in the U.K. Rather, the videos show Shiite Muslims marking Ashura, the culmination of 10 days of mourning to mark the martyrdom of Husayn ibn Ali, the grandson of the prophet Muhammad, on June 21.
According to the Encyclopedia Britannica, Shiite Muslims mark this day with assemblies such as the one seen in the video that feature, "sermons, poetry, chest-beating, and passion plays reenacting Husayn's martyrdom."
The Ashura assembly on the "Curry Mile" is an annual event in Manchester that local news media has covered for more than 10 years. The Manchester Evening news called the event a "ritual self-flagellation procession" in 2015 but did not report that the people participating called themselves "Soldiers of Allah" or demanded Shariah be imposed in the U.K.
The source of the video that circulated in November was unclear, though at least two of the clips featured (at 0:06 and 0:16) camefrom a separate video (at 1:20 and 1:59, archived) posted on Instagram by 
Murtaza Ali Shah, a journalist for a Pakistani news outlet.
Shah confirmed to Snopes via Instagram he recorded the footage and it showed the Ashura event in Manchester in June.
In addition to misrepresenting what the video showed, the social media post above also made a false claim about the alleged "Soldiers of Allah" calling for Shariah in the U.K.
The poster wrote (emphasis ours): "A large group of military-age men took to the streets in a Manchester suburb calling themselves soldiers of Allah and demanding sharia law be put in place because they now form the majority in the neighborhood."
Manchester, where the June Ashura assembly took place, is not majority Muslim. According to the latest U.K. Ccensus data from 2021, 22.3% of people — less than one in four — within the Manchester City Council governance area identified as Muslims. Rusholme, where the "Curry Mile" is located, is part of Manchester City Council. According to census data, 38.5% of people in the Rusholme East census area, which borders the "Curry Mile," identified as Muslim.
For further reading, Snopes previously investigated whether a video showed U.K. shoppers standing in gender-segregated lines and another video of Shiite Muslims marking Ashura in Dearborn, Michigan.

New Delhi: India has initiated inter-ministerial deliberations on a possible review of its liberalized wheat export policy, just three months after allowing unrestricted overseas shipments of the grain, as it assesses domestic production for the current crop year through June 2027, said two people aware of the matter.
The discussions follow a sharp slowdown in wheat sowing and concerns over soil moisture after the southwest monsoon ended with a 13% rainfall deficit this year. Wheat acreage stood at 5.007million hectares (mn ha.) as of 13 November, down 15.3% from 5.910 mn ha. a year earlier, according to the latest available data from the agriculture ministry.
The government is assessing domestic wheat availability, food security requirements and the availability of water for irrigation before taking a view on the existing export policy, said the first of the two persons cited earlier, both speaking on condition of anonymity.
“The discussions are at an initial stage and are precautionary in nature, given the decline in wheat acreage and its potential impact on production. However, this does not mean that the government is moving towards restricting exports,” said the second person.
“Since sowing is still underway, a decision will be taken at an appropriate time after considering all relevant factors and keeping farmers' interests in mind,” said the second person.
Queries sent to the spokespersons of the ministry of consumer affairs, food and public distribution, as well as the secretary, department of food and public distribution, on Monday remained unanswered till press time.
Periodic bans
India has banned wheat exports periodically in recent decades to ensure adequate domestic supplies and keep a lid on prices. India banned wheat exports in 2007 to curb a price rise and lifted the ban only in September 2011 after successive years of good harvests. It again prohibited wheat shipments in May 2022 and eased restriction on overseas despatches in February 2026 before lifting the ban altogether in August 2026. The country, however, has allowed government-to-government deals in limited quantities to accede to diplomatic requests even while keeping a generalised ban on wheat exports.
The latest sowing figures have raised questions about the outlook for the next wheat harvest, particularly as water availability and soil moisture conditions remain important determinants of crop development.
Industry experts said that Indian wheat is currently relatively expensive in the international market, limiting the immediate commercial incentive for exports.
"At the moment, export of wheat is not a lucrative proposition as international wheat prices are currently very low, partly due to the depreciation of the dollar and appreciation of the rupee. Also, supplies from the Black Sea region, particularly Russia and Ukraine, are keeping global prices subdued. In India, wheat prices are largely governed by the minimum support price (MSP), which is relatively high and keeps prices elevated. Unlike domestic prices, international prices are driven primarily by market forces of demand and supply," said Navneet Chitlangia, former president of the Roller Flour Millers' Federation of India.
"At present, we are not receiving enquiries from international wheat buyers, possibly because Indian wheat is not competitively priced in the global market. The price parity gap between domestic and international markets appears to be discouraging buyers, as global wheat prices remain lower, making Indian supplies relatively expensive for overseas importers," said Varun Verma, proprietor of Delhi-based Nidhiraj Exports.
Substantial stocks
The government currently has substantial wheat stocks in its central pool, providing a cushion against near-term supply concerns.
According to the Food Corporation of India (FCI), which procures and stores foodgrains from farmers, wheat stocks in the central pool stood at 447.60 lakh tonnes as of 1 November, compared with the prescribed minimum quantity of 20.520 million tonnes (mt) for 1 October. The stocks were also significantly higher than the 30.727mt held on 1 November 2025.
The central pool stocks comprise grain held by the FCI and state government agencies.
However, the stock position will need to be assessed alongside procurement requirements for the next marketing season and the government's foodgrain distribution commitments.
Under the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY), eligible beneficiaries covered under the National Food Security Act (NFSA) receive 5kg of free foodgrains per person per month under Priority Households (PHH) and 35kg per household per month for Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) families. This free foodgrain distribution arrangement has been extended until December 2028.
For FY27, the government has allocated 21.855mt of wheat for distribution and sale, around 2.7mt higher than it did in FY26. Of the total, 21.447mt has been earmarked for distribution under the National Food Security Act and the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana, up from 17.133mt in the previous fiscal.
This assumes significance as the government seeks to balance rising distribution requirements with adequate buffer stocks amid the risk of lower wheat production. It has set an initial procurement target of 30.3mt for the 2026-27 marketing season, marginally lower than 31.0mt targeted for the previous season (2025-26).

Imagine having a medicine that could help manage your child’s rare genetic condition, but being unable to afford it because a year’s treatment costs as much as ₹9 crore. For seven families in India, that situation could soon change.
Seven children diagnosed with Allan-Herndon-Dudley syndrome (AHDS), a rare genetic disorder, are set to receive a year’s supply of the medicine tiratricol free of cost on November 30, following an initiative led by Hyderabad-based paediatrician Dr. Sivaranjani Santosh and Access to Medicines India.
The development is significant not just because the families will receive the medicine without paying for it, but also because its cost has been brought down through pharmaceutical compounding in the Netherlands. While the commercial version of the drug costs approximately ₹4.68 crore to ₹9 crore per child annually, the compounded formulation is estimated to cost just ₹2.5 lakh per child for a year.
The medicine has been prepared by Transvaal Pharmacy in The Hague, Netherlands, with support from the Netherlands-based Pharmaceutical Accountability Foundation (PAF). The first batch will be handed over to the parents of the seven children along with the necessary documentation and individual import permissions. The families have secured approvals for one year of treatment. As the compounded medicine has a shelf life of six months, it will be imported in two batches.
How did a ₹9-crore treatment become available for ₹2.5 lakh?
The initiative began after Arav, a child under the care of Dr. Sivaranjani, was diagnosed with AHDS, also known as MCT8 deficiency. The condition is caused by mutations affecting the MCT8 gene, which plays an important role in transporting thyroid hormones into brain cells. Tiratricol, also known as TRIAC, acts on thyroid hormone receptors and may help overcome some effects of the deficiency. It also helps minimise complications associated with peripheral thyrotoxicosis.
Although the medicine was available in Europe, its commercial price put it beyond the reach of most Indian families. Arav’s mother, Pavitra Sirolkar, had to arrange approximately ₹12 lakh to ₹13 lakh for just one month’s supply of the medicine from Germany. Dr. Sivaranjani initially approached paediatricians, endocrinologists and paediatric neurologists to explore ways of procuring the drug. Doctors at Christian Medical College (CMC), Vellore, where five other children with the same condition had been identified, were also approached.
Attempts to obtain the medicine through pharmaceutical company Egetis Therapeutics and its compassionate-use programme did not succeed. The situation eventually prompted Dr. Sivaranjani to take the issue to social media. On September 7, she posted an appeal seeking help for the family and urged people to tag the Prime Minister, Union Health Minister and other government representatives. The appeal gained attention, bringing it to the notice of PAF.
The foundation subsequently explored the possibility of preparing the medicine through pharmaceutical compounding using the active pharmaceutical ingredient. Transvaal Pharmacy conducted test batches and developed a formulation for the seven children. The initial group included Arav and five children receiving treatment at CMC Vellore. A seventh child, aged one year, was identified after his father contacted Dr Sivaranjani following her social media appeal.
Who is funding the treatment?
According to PAF, the total cost of providing one year’s treatment to all seven children is €14,200, approximately ₹15.08 lakh. Of this, Dr Sivaranjani raised approximately ₹6.09 lakh in India, while PAF undertook to raise the remaining €8,600, approximately ₹9.13 lakh, in the Netherlands. The medicine will be provided to all seven families free of cost.
Will the medicine become available in India?
While the November 30 handover addresses the immediate treatment requirements of the seven children, Dr. Sivaranjani believes that importing the medicine cannot be a permanent solution. She plans to approach the Union government and work with Access to Medicines India and other organisations to explore the possibility of getting the medicine compounded in India and making it accessible to more children.
“How can a medicine be available in the world but not be available for our children? We should get the medicine compounded in India and make it available for all the children with this condition,” she said.

Two attacks in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) have killed 4 workers responding to the Ebola outbreak and injured 5 others.
The attacks occurred overnight on a shared living camp in Biakato Mines and an Ebola response coordination office in Mangina.
“We are heartbroken that people have died in the line of duty as they worked to save others,” said Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, World Health Organization Director-General. “The world has lost brave professionals.”
The dead include a member of a vaccination team, two drivers and a police officer. No WHO staff are among those killed, one staff member was injured.
“My heart goes out to the family and friends of the first responders killed in these attacks,” said Dr Matshidiso Moeti, WHO Regional Director for Africa. “We are doing everything possible to bring the injured and front-line workers in the impacted areas to safety. These constant attacks must stop. We will continue to work with the DRC Government, partners and MONUSCO to ensure the security of our staff and other health workers.”
In the last week, there were 7 cases of Ebola, down from a peak of over 120 per week in April 2019.
“Ebola was retreating. These attacks will give it force again, and more people will die as a consequence,” said Dr Tedros. “It will be tragic to see more unnecessary suffering in communities that have already suffered so much. We call on everyone who has a role to play to end this cycle of violence.”
The situation is still evolving. WHO will provide updates as new information comes in.

Fact Check
In order to determine the veracity of these claims, first, we ran a reverse image search on some of the keyframes of the viral clip. This led us to images of a restaurant called Durbin Bangla located in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

Cameron Smith plots pathway back to the PGA Tour after moving on from LIV Golf
Cameron Smith joined LIV Golf in 2022 after clinching his first major at The Open at St Andrews; the Australian will play select events on the DP World Tour in 2027; watch Smith in action at this week's BMW Australian PGA Championship live on Sky Sports
Tuesday 24 November 2026 07:49, UK
Cameron Smith has moved on from LIV Golf, is preparing for his invitation-only appearances on the DP World Tour and is already thinking about a return to the PGA Tour.
As the 2022 Open champion prepared for the BMW Australian PGA Championship starting Thursday at The Lakes in Sydney, attention inevitably turned to his career goals and his steps toward a possible return to the PGA Tour.
"I guess that's the path. That's where I want to be now for sure," Smith told the Australian Associated Press.
"DP's given us a chance to kind of fulfil that. We'll see how that goes. There's plenty of good players out there and plenty of other guys that want to do the same thing, so it's going to be difficult.
"But for sure that's where I want to play."
How can Smith return to the PGA Tour?
Smith will not return as a full-time member on the DP World Tour, but is one of a number of former LIV players, including Dustin Johnson and Bubba Watson, to sign an agreement with the tour to receive invites to a specific number of tournaments during the 2027 season, excluding Rolex Series events.
He receives an exemption to play this week, having won the BMW Australian PGA Championship three times in 2017, 2018 and 2022.
Under the DP World Tour and PGA Tour's current agreement, the top 10 players on the Race to Dubai Rankings qualify for the PGA Tour.
The number of PGA Tour cards available to players finishing at the top of the Race to Dubai Rankings for the 2028 season is yet to be determined, with the PGA Tour set to launch its new two-tier championship structure the year after next.
However, to even have a chance at winning one of those coveted cards, Smith will need to play more tournaments on the DP World Tour's 2027 schedule.
He could do that by winning the co-sanctioned BMW Australian PGA Championship or the Australian Open at Kingston Heath, which begins on December 3 and also features Rory McIlroy.
"I think given what they've told me, I pretty much need to win this year to get membership," Smith said.
"It's all still very blurry to me at the moment. There are a lot of rules, but we'll have a few opportunities, and like I said, I've always managed to play pretty good down here, so why not start it off with a good one?"
The PGA Tour board last week said it had "thoughtful discussions" about the future of players at LIV Golf but otherwise seemed to be in no hurry to decide if there is room for them next season.
CEO Brian Rolapp said the Returning Member Program, which allowed Brooks Koepka to return to the PGA Tour at the beginning of 2026 with financial penalties, was not on the table.
Smith didn't take up that one-time offer in January, which applied only to players who'd won majors or The Players Championship from 2022 through 2025, which included himself, Koepka, Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau.
'It was a big move to go to LIV'
Smith is in a kind of limbo. LIV Golf, which lost the financial support of Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) and filed for bankruptcy on September 8, told a bankruptcy court earlier this month it had abandoned plans for a new version of the league and had begun winding down its business.
"There was a lot of uncertainty and then in a way it was good to just like get the noise over and done with," Smith, who joined LIV after winning The Open at St Andrews in 2022, said.
"It was a big move to go LIV at the start for sure, and I think everyone that was close to me and all my friends saw why I was doing it and why I made the decision."
Adam Scott said he had no doubts about Smith fitting back in.
"Cam's incredibly talented and he'll adjust to his new environment," Scott said. "He'll be just fine."
How to watch the BMW Australian PGA Championship?
The DP World Tour kicks off its 2027 season at the BMW Australian PGA Championship at The Lakes Golf Club in Sydney, Australia, on Thursday, and you can watch all four rounds live on Sky Sports.
Coverage of Thursday's first round begins at 1am on Sky Sports Golf and Sky Sports Main Event, while Friday's second round will be shown live at 1am on Sky Sports Golf.

Parts of Bangladesh were shut down Thursday as protests by supporters of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina sparked clashes, bomb blasts and arson attacks, with the ancestral home of former leader Muhammad Yunus set ablaze in the violence.
Hasina’s Awami League party had called for a week-long programme of protests and rallies to mobilise support for Hasina’s planned return in December, culminating in a nationwide lockdown on Thursday.
Hasina, who has lived in exile in neighbouring India since she fled Dhaka following violent protests demanding her resignation in August 2024, has requested a new passport and identity card to facilitate her return. Her supporters are protesting against the government’s rejection of that request.
To deter violence, 97 platoons of the Bangladesh Border Guard fanned out across seven districts, including Gopalganj and Faridpur, considered to have many Hasina supporters, a spokesperson said.
Police said former interim leader Yunus’ ancestral home in Chattogram, about 300km (186 miles) south-east of Dhaka, was set on fire late on Wednesday.
It is likely that flammable substances were thrown into an unused ground-floor room, police told Reuters, adding that Yunus’ paternal family members, who live on the upper floors, are safe.
Reuters could not immediately reach the Yunus Centre thinktank that speaks on his behalf to seek comment. Yunus and his government, which led Bangladesh after Hasina’s ouster, have faced hostility from her supporters.
During the last 10 days of protests, police have reported dozens of crude bomb blasts and incidents of vehicles being set afire in at least 28 districts, injuring several police officials and members of the public, media have said.
Late on Tuesday, an activist of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist party (BNP) was allegedly killed by unidentified people during a protest near Hasina’s home district of Gopalganj, police said.
On the same night, a crude bomb exploded outside the Dhaka residence of cultural affairs minister Nitai Roy Chowdhury, and the house of a BNP lawmaker and shops belonging to BNP supporters in Gopalganj were set on fire, police added.
On Wednesday morning, a bus company helper was burnt to death in the southern district of Pirojpur after two buses were set on fire, authorities said.
Tuesday marks a year since Hasina was sentenced to death by a local court that found her guilty of ordering a deadly crackdown on a student-led uprising against her in 2024. She has lived in exile in neighbouring India since fleeing Dhaka.
On Thursday, authorities detained former education minister Nurul Islam Nahid, who faces charges over several killings during the 2024 protests, from his house in Dhaka, police told Reuters.
At least 37 branches and offices of Grameen Bank, set up by Yunus, have been targeted in arson attacks or attempted fires since 10 November, with 14 more attacked since midnight on Tuesday, the bank said.
On Tuesday, the home minister Salahuddin Ahmed accused Awami League leaders abroad of inciting supporters to destabilise Bangladesh and torch property, adding that those involved in violence would be identified and prosecuted.
Awami League leaders, most of them in hiding, could not be reached for comment.

The Department of Medical Education is preparing to start two new government medical colleges in Ramanagara of Bengaluru South District and Puttur of Dakshina Kannada District for the academic year of 2027-28, and a proposal will be submitted to the National Medical Commission (NMC) soon.
“The construction work for the medical college on the Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences (RGUHS) new campus in Ramanagara is progressing rapidly. The tender for the medical college in Puttur has been finalised, and the construction will commence shortly. We will apply to the NMC to start these colleges from 2027-28 with a capacity of at least 50 seats,” Medical Education Minister Sharan Prakash Patil said.
“There is also a proposal to start medical colleges in Vijayapura and Kolar districts. The cabinet will decide on that soon,” he added.
The government has decided to start a medical college in every district of the State. There are 25 now. If colleges are established in Ramanagara, Puttur, Vijayapura, and Kolar districts, only Tumakuru, Bengaluru Rural, and Udupi districts will have to have a government medical college of their own.
Currently, there are 76 medical colleges in the State, comprising 25 government and 51 private institutions, with a total of 15,745 seats available for the 2026-27 academic year. If the Ramanagara and Puttur colleges are approved for the next academic year, with 50 seats each, this will go up to 78 colleges with 15,845 seats.
Will NMC approve this year?
The NMC has rejected the State’s applications for starting medical colleges in Kanakapura and Ramanagara four times from 2023-24 to 2026-27, for want of infrastructure, including teaching and non-teaching staff. Will the commission approve the proposals this year at least is the moot question.
In this context, the State government decided to construct a medical college and hospital in Kanakapura at an estimated cost of about ₹550 crore, and the construction work is in progress. However, the work of the medical college planned to be built on the proposed Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences (RGUHS) campus in Ramanagara is only 70% complete. Therefore, the government has decided to start the medical college using the district hospital.
“The construction of medical college on the RGUHS new campus in Ramanagara will be completed soon. Consequently, steps have been taken to shift the university to the new campus within the next three to four months. Meanwhile, the construction of a medical college and hospital in Kanakapura is progressing rapidly, and once the work is complete, a proposal will be submitted to the MNC for the commencement of the college,” Mr. Patil said.

Dhaka, Nov 24: Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return home from exile in India on December 16, the day the country celebrates as Victory Day when it won independence after a war with Pakistan.
Hasina went into exile in India on August 5, 2024, after a student-led mass uprising forced her to end her 15-year rule. She was sentenced to death in absentia for crimes against humanity involving the uprising in which hundreds of protesters were killed. Hasina rejected the verdict and has said she is ready fight the case once she is back.
In the statement Tuesday announcing the planned date of her return, she urged current Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to arrange her return on the national airline.
“Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5th, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka,” spokesman Syed Mozammel Ali said in the statement.
“It is deeply symbolic that she has chosen 16 December, our Victory Day, for her planned return to Bangladesh. We firmly believe that she will celebrate this historic day among her people, honouring the great victory achieved under the leadership of her father, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman," Abu Obaidha Arin, an aide to Hasina, told The Associated Press.
“We are equally confident that, she will definitely return and under her leadership post return, Bangladesh will once again advance towards peace, stability and prosperity,” Arin said.
Earlier this month, in an interview with The Associated Press, Hasina said she would return to the country in December at any cost, and even death could not prevent her from returning home.

These dead pets were meant to be cremated - then their bodies appeared on a livestream
- Published
The livestream begins.
A man – bald, goateed, wearing red-tinted sunglasses – walks down a cracked back road, guiding the camera towards a cluster of plastic-wrapped objects that spill out of the tall grass.
Names are written on the packages – Brandon; Ira; Lucky; Sweet – and numbers. One says 29kg (4.5 stone). Another says 2.5kg. Through the plastic you can make out what appears to be fur, claws and a flattened ear.
It's a mass dumping, the man explains. "We have about 25 animals here that have been dumped in bags. A couple of cats, some dogs."
"Purebreds," says the woman filming.
Warning: This story contains images some might find upsetting
In the weeks since that video was streamed on Facebook, Chris and Geraldine Taylor, who run animal rescue NGO Luna and Furry Siblings (LAFS), say they have uncovered 15 dumping sites in the suburbs of Bulacan, near the Philippines' capital of Manila.
In total they've unearthed the remains of some 170 dead pets. Belgian Malinois, golden retrievers, pugs, puppies and cats have been found dumped off service roads, sealed in septic tanks, floating in rivers and buried in vacant lots.
Many of these animals are thought to have been sent to cremation businesses in the expectation they would be turned to ash.
Now, many grieving owners are having to confront a distressing reality: their beloved pets may not have received the send-off they paid for. The urn in their home may not contain their pet at all. And they may in fact see their so-called fur child again, jettisoned like common waste on the side of a highway.
One saw the livestream and wrote on Facebook: "I think one of those pets is mine." Below, they attached a photo of a beaming Alsatian.
170 carcasses found
When Chris arrived on that back road three weeks ago, he couldn't have known he was uncorking a scandal that would see at least one business reportedly shut, four people placed under investigation, and a personal invite to sit down with a senator to discuss animal-cruelty laws.
Chris, a former police officer, and his wife are retired, but only formally. For the past three years, they've been running an animal rescue shelter out of their home in San Jose del Monte, 30km (18.6 miles) north-east of central Manila.
On 30 October, he'd driven into town to report a case of animal neglect at the local district office. When he arrived, he was told the official in charge had just left to respond to another complaint: a report of dumped animals on a nearby roadside.
Chris had seen this once before: 14 dogs that were found and soon reburied. This time, he followed the official to the scene and started documenting – taking photos, scanning the bodies for microchips and uploading footage to his Facebook page.
"I figured there's got to be more to this," he explains. "So we put out word: if anybody knows anything, any other dump locations... just report it. Let us know."
In the days that followed, tip-offs started trickling in. More dumpsites emerged.
"The long vacant lot on the left side... that's where the smell comes from," read one message.
"When we ran to this place it smelled of rotting animals," read another, accompanied by a photo of a map with a location circled in red.
By crowdsourcing intel in this way, and collaborating with authorities, LAFS has so far uncovered a total of 15 dumpsites, containing an estimated 170 animals. "Some of them were just bags of bones," Chris says. "Others were liquefied."
LAFS has meticulously documented the crime scenes. Often wearing little more for protection than an N95 mask and rubber gloves, Chris crouches in the underbrush and slices open discarded plastic bags, picking through the contents while Geraldine holds the camera.
Their Facebook videos have racked up more than 30 million views. Commenters ask Chris if he has seen their pet among the bodies, or if he can turn a carcass over so they can check for identifying marks.
Some are successful. On that first night in October, all 25 bodies were returned to their owners.
There's a question which hangs uncomfortably over every dumpsite: who would do something like this?
As more owners came forward, a common denominator emerged. Many said they'd taken the animals to be incinerated at the same place: a crematorium called Ahjay Paws in the city of Bacoor, not far from Manila.
"So I posted: anybody that's had Ahjay's services... these might be your animals," says Chris. "And man, it just flooded in."
'God knows what was inside those urns'
The Philippines has long been a dog-loving nation, but since the Covid-19 pandemic the "fur parenting" community has exploded.
A 2021 study found the country had the highest rate of dog ownership in the Asia-Pacific. Since then, the pet dog population has increased 4.7% year on year, according to another study, exceeding 21 million in 2025.
As the numbers soar, businesses have stepped up to address an inevitable implication: more deaths.
"Cremation here in the Philippines has become quite a big thing with the boom of the pet industry," says Anna Cabrera, director at the Philippine Animal Welfare Society (Paws). "There's even a ceremony where they hold wakes for the pets."
These events offer grieving owners a last chance to see their beloved pets before they're taken to a crematorium and transmuted into an urnful of ashes.
Or not, as the case may be.
Revecca Calling, who lives south of Bulacan in the city of Cavite, says she paid Ahjay Paws 8,500 Philippine pesos (£100; $133) to cremate her dog Olaf in January. The price was calculated according to weight, and included a 30-minute viewing where she could say her final goodbye.
Calling says Ahjay Paws told her they couldn't record the cremation, as it might endanger the staff. They took away Olaf's body, and a few days later handed back a small urn that purportedly contained her cremated remains.
When nine months later Calling heard that dozens of animals' bodies had been found dumped on an empty plot of land, potentially at the behest of a pet cremation business, she was devastated.
"Pet owners entrust these services with something very important: the remains of a beloved family member," she says. "We need to know what happened."
Earlier this month, the Philippines' National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) filed criminal complaints against four individuals in connection with dumped pets. Among them is the owner of Ahjay Paws and two people who ran Bulacan's Pet HPHT Crematory.
According to the NBI, Ahjay Paws had initially arranged to acquire a cremation machine from Pet HPHT – but when it didn't arrive, they opted to send the pet remains to Pet HPHT instead. When the volume of those remains became more than Pet HPHT could handle, that firm paid a third party to bury them.
One interpretation is that the dumping incidents are a result of logistical failures: two businesses that bit off more than they could chew and took desperate measures to make the problem go away.
But there's another theory: that the dead pets could be evidence of a lucrative racket, with people's money taken to incinerate their pets but the animals then being dumped instead.
There is a word for this kind of deception in Philippine law – estafa; where a perpetrator knowingly misleads a victim to financially defraud them – and the NBI say they are investigating it as a possibility in this case.
Two weeks ago, Ahjay Paws' owner denied responsibility for the dumping in San Jose del Monte, according to local media. The company is apparently no longer operating, and the BBC has been unable to contact it.
The BBC has also reached out to Pet HPHT and invited it to respond. On Facebook, the firm said the dumping allegations were "completely false and have no basis".
Another grieving pet owner, Emelia Legada, says she paid Ahjay Paws 10,000 Philippine pesos (£120; $160) to cremate her dog Harvey six months ago.
"I just can't accept the pain of not knowing what might have happened to him," she says. "I really want to confirm whether Harvey was properly cremated, and whether the ashes I received were truly his."
Many are wrestling with the same uncertainty. As Cabrera puts it: "God knows what that was inside those urns."
In response to those anxieties, a veterinarian in nearby Quezon City has started offering complimentary forensic ash testing. For those whose pets have been found among the bodies, other crematoriums have offered to do the job properly, and for free.
The animal welfare society, Paws, is volunteering legal services to help people file complaints with the authorities, and has received more than 150 requests so far. It is also calling for a nationwide audit of all pet cremation businesses.
Animal-cruelty law 'doesn't apply'
On 2 November, Percival Vilar Cendaña of the Philippines' progressive Akbayan Party appeared on national television. He was there to speak about the pet-dumping scandal, which, in the span of a few days, had flared into a national disgrace.
"Our worst fears have been confirmed," he told the Bilyonaryo news channel. "Now we see that these are not isolated incidents. It is true that this is a syndicate that is conducting widespread operations."
Neither the police nor the NBI have confirmed that the dumpings were carried out by a "syndicate", nor that they were "widespread". Many details surrounding the case remain murky. But the hysteria is real – and Cendaña was giving voice to a common sentiment.
"Those who deceived these poor fur parents should be jailed," he said.
At least three individuals have surrendered to the NBI and been charged with violating the city's Code of Sanitation, the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act, and the Sanitation Code of the Philippines.
But many feel this doesn't go far enough, and say it fails to hold anyone liable for the way the animals' remains were treated.
Cabrera says the country's animal-cruelty law doesn't cover the treatment of animals after death. And "there's no crime if there's no law".
The scandal has prompted a groundswell to change that. Lawmakers like Cendaña are pushing for a national commission on animal welfare to ensure their dignity in life and death.
Meanwhile, Cabrera says Paws will seek "moral and exemplary" damages on behalf of aggrieved pet owners.
One woman whose dog was suspected to have been found among the dumped bodies told the BBC she couldn't speak about it because she was "feeling weak".
"I haven't slept for three days from all the crying," she said.
Chris has also been losing sleep, taking calls from grieving pet owners who have watched his videos. "Hundreds of people call me in tears, just sobbing," he says.
"They're in so much pain. And half the time you're telling them: 'you're not going to find your pet. It's been too long; we're not going to be able to identify it.' And it just crushes them."
As well as new laws, Chris wants stricter enforcement of existing rules. He wants to know how he managed to unearth so much in the space of a fortnight, and why people keep coming to him saying they don't trust the police to take their concerns seriously, he says.
The BBC contacted Philippine National Police (PNP) for comment, but didn't hear back. Earlier this month, PNP chief Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr said authorities were determined to hold accountable those who allegedly took advantage of grieving pet owners, saying such exploitation "must be addressed with the full force of the law", according to ABS-CBN.
"Fraud is not measured solely by the amount of money taken, but also by the damage inflicted on the people whose trust has been betrayed," Nartatez said.
"To the affected pet owners, we recognise the pain and distress this incident has caused your families."
Yet the police themselves have come under official scrutiny.
On Monday, the National Police Commission announced an investigation into officers in Cavite and Bulacan after they suggested LAFS might be involved in the pet dumping because they were often first on the scene. The officers did not present evidence for their claims. The investigation also covers reports that officers visited the Taylors' home and took photographs.
Meanwhile, countless grieving pet owners are suspended in purgatory: desperate for closure on what happened to their dogs and cats, and calling on authorities to do more.
"We want the case to be properly investigated and those responsible to be held accountable," says Calling. "I believe that no secret remains hidden forever."
Legada, for her part, says: "I just want to find out what really happened to Harvey and where his remains are. I want to know whether he was properly cremated."
She also wants people to know: "You can't trust anyone these days."

When discussing cervical cancer, what often gets left out is that it is one of the most preventable of cancers. Despite this, cervical cancer continues to be a cause of thousands of deaths among women every year, not only in India, but in many parts of the world. In many such cases, the condition is detected far too late, leaving limited room for intervention. The issue therefore, is not a gap in science, but a gap in awareness
The main culprit in cervical cancer is a virus that is very common, human papillomavirus, or HPV for short. HPV primarily spreads through close skin-to-skin contact, most often during sexual intercourse. The virus is so widespread that virtually everyone, both men and women, at some point in their lifetime, will be infected without even realising it. More often than not, the immune system gets rid of the virus without causing any damage.

GTA 6 player gets social ban on PSN after sending a photo of in-game nudity
Apparently just because it’s in the game doesn’t mean sharing “obscene” content is okay.
Grand Theft Auto 6 has dominated everyone's attention since it came out last week and broke the record for the most day one retail sales in entertainment history. Unfortunately, not everyone's experience has been 100 percent positive, especially now that one player has been hit with a social ban on PSN after sharing a photo of naked people taken with the game's built-in camera feature.
According to X user @derrickgott007, they received a notice from PlayStation Safety saying their account was being temporarily suspended from using social features for 30 days after breaching the company's code of conduct regarding pornographic or obscene content. The issue is that the user claims the offending image was actually a photo taken using GTA 6's camera feature of a nudist resort they found inside the game before sharing it with someone else on PSN.
In this case, if you simply go by what's outlined in PlayStation's code of conduct, technically this player did break the rules as there's a specific bullet point about not sharing, soliciting, accessing, distributing or storing "material that is obscene, pornographic, or illegal." However, where things get a bit murky is that the source of the offending material came from a game being played on a PS5 that is also sold digitally by Sony itself. This feels a bit hypocritical as it seems that it's okay for a game to contain nudity or pornographic material, but as soon as you take a photo or screenshot of said content, suddenly you're in violation of PlayStation's guidelines.
Furthermore, while a social ban might not sound that bad as the user will still have access to some games, because online multiplayer falls under the umbrella of social activity, @derrickgott007 says they can't even play Call of Duty during their 30-day suspension.
Another interesting topic that incidents like this bring up is how often regular people agree to things they haven't fully read or acknowledged due to a company's terms of service (ToS) or end-user license agreement (EULA). Often, these documents are so long and onerous that people blindly skip past them and hit the checkbox just so they can use the thing they paid for. Some organizations like the ToS;DR project have made efforts to call out companies with terms of services that are unnecessarily dense or difficult to understand, but it remains an ongoing issue for almost everyone in modern society.
Sadly, even though PlayStation's guidelines seem a bit contradictory, this incident should serve as a public service announcement to anyone considering taking a photo or screenshot of potentially obscene material in GTA 6 (or other games) with their PS5, as they need to be extra careful or else they risk getting hit with a similar ban.

Quick Answer
From its origins as a racing game called Race ‘n’ Chase to billion-dollar sales records, GTA has a fascinating history. Here are 11 surprising facts about the franchise, including Hollywood connections, hidden ghosts, clever anti-piracy tricks, celebrity lawsuits, and its Scottish roots.
After more than a decade of waiting, Rockstar Games has finally launched perhaps the most anticipated game in the recent history of gaming. Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6). It has been barely a few days since the game hit the stands and the Web, and it already has the world (gaming and non-gaming too) in its grip, and is setting sales records.
Its release means saying goodbye to the legendary “we got (this/something) before GTA 6” meme, but GTA 6 is already carving a place for itself in the franchise’s history, a history marked by crime, cars, and chaos and a lot of other things that even diehard fans might not be aware of.
From celebrity lawsuits to ghosts and many controversies, the world of GTA is filled with insane stories. So even as you set yourself up for another session of GTA 6 or wait for your copy of the game to download, or just turn your nose up at “crazy gamers who will line up for anything”, here are eleven amazing facts you might not know (but should know) about the legendary Grand Theft Auto franchise.
Table of Contents
It was originally supposed to be a racing game (and called Race’n’Chase)
It may look completely different today, but GTA was originally supposed to be a fast-paced, addictive racing game called “Race ‘n’ Chase.” Development of the game got underway in the mid-nineties, but the developers did not quite get things right. Early models had car-crashing issues and coding glitches that made police cars ram into player cars aggressively, instead of just chasing them. This, of course, took away its traditional racing game feel. But during testing, players enjoyed this glitch and chaos, so the developers decided to move away from a “Race n Chase” sort of setup and decided to create an open world action-oriented game. They called it Grand Theft Auto (GTA). The rest, as they love to say, is history.
Play the OG GTA online and free of cost
Want to experience the original Grand Theft Auto that was released in 1997? Well, you can actually play it for free online in a browser at https://www.playdosgames.com/online/grand-theft-auto/. Just make sure you have a keyboard handy, as it struggles with touch controls.
Thank you, Tony Montana! GTA: Vice City was inspired by Scarface!
Even the greatest video games have to draw inspiration from somewhere, and in the case of GTA: Vice City, inspiration came from Brian De Palma’s 1983 crime classic, Scarface. The developers used the movie as a blueprint to showcase how Miami looked back in the 80s. The protagonist in the game also follows a very similar arc to the protagonist in the film, the iconic Tony Montana, and even has a location similar to that of Tony Montana’s (Scarface’s protagonist) infamous mansion in it.
GTA has a lot of Hollywood in it…but is not too fond of stars
GTA has not just drawn inspiration from Hollywood, but has also featured many famous actors from it. The game has cast a number of actors, comedians, and musicians to either play themselves or voice a character. A key reason for hiring musicians and comedians to play themselves in the game or be a part of an extensive radio or DJ set is to make the city in the game feel even more real and lived in. Famous actors like Ray Liotta, Samuel L. Jackson, Burt Reynolds, and many more have been a part of the franchise. This tradition lives on with GTA 6, as this time around actors Dylan Rourke and Manni Perez have voiced the two leads of the game.
That said, problems with a number of high-profile stars (most notably Burt Reynolds) led Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser to say in an interview with Vulture “We don’t bring in name actors anymore because of their egos and, most important of all, because we believe we get a better sense of immersion using talented actors whose voices you don’t recognize.”
The Ghost Town of GTA 3 that is ‘out of bounds’
Imagine having a small part of the game that you cannot explore? Well, that is exactly what the Ghost Town in GTA 3 is. It has nothing to do with gameplay, lacks the general collision mechanism of the game, and yet it exists. The ‘out of bounds’ area was actually designed as part of GTA 3’s opening cinematics and was put away from the main map, and kept in the game only for the intro scene. However, players found their way to the location using glitches and modifications, although they could not interact with it like the rest of the game. Before Vice City, there was Ghost City in the GTAverse.
Punishing pirates, the GTA way
By the time GTA 4 was released in 2008, the GTA franchise had become insanely famous. And with great celebrity and terrific sales comes…great piracy. As pirated and unauthorized units of the game became a problem, Rockstar Games used some very creative countermeasures to punish/ annoy those who bought pirated copies of the game. Unauthorized copies ended up with constant drunk effects on the camera, sudden and auto acceleration, broken mission scripts, damaged cars, and more, which were put in place to make the pirated game actually feel pirated. You do not pirate a gangster game easily!
Macabre and moving Easter eggs
The GTA franchise is laden with Easter eggs, but two of the most amazing ones are found in GTA 5. What makes them special is the attention to both detail and sentiment. These are not your run-of-the-mill “press this key and your car changes into Superman” or “use this key combo to start driving on Mars” kinds of easter eggs, but much more somber and sensitive ones.
In GTA 5 between 23:00 and 00:00, you can actually find a translucent figure at the peak of Mount Gordo. There is a flat rock where the ghost of “Jolene Cranley-Evans,” who was said to have been killed by her husband, Jock Cranley, appears around midnight. Jock had pushed her off the mountain peak, which is also why, when the player goes near the ghost, it disappears and “Jock” written in blood appears on the flat rock!
The other Easter egg is not as eerie but definitely heartbreaking. A small dog can be seen sitting quietly next to the grave of his owner in the Pacific Bluffs cemetery between 10:00 am and 11:00 am. This is the game paying tribute to a real grieving dog, Greyfriars Bobby, a 19th-century dog who guarded his owner’s grave for 14 years.
Watch the moon in GTA 5!
It was not just the easter eggs that were amazing in GTA 5. Rockstar Games upped their detail game (pun intended) by several notches, paying attention to the tiniest of details. The best example of this is the moon in the game. Yes, the moon. The moon in GTA 5 does not remain the same through the gameplay and actually goes through proper lunar phases– something many players might not even notice during regular gameplay. So you get full, crescent, waxing gibbous, and other phases of the moon while playing the game. Now, that’s one moonshot that worked.
GTA and controversies go hand in hand, and even the Guinness Book agrees
Ever since its release in 1997, the GTA franchise has been surrounded by controversies. And these have only gotten bigger with each new version. Celebrities like Lindsay Lohan, Karen Gravano, Michael Washington have filed lawsuits against Rockstar Games’ parent company Take-Two Interactive, for modeling its characters on them.
The game has also attracted a lot of criticism for its alleged glorification of violence and sexual themes – GTA: San Andreas was hit by the Hot Coffee controversy in 2004, when developers left explicit, sexual interactive code in the game instead of deleting it. They had disabled the code, but players used mods to access it, which allowed them to make the main character (CJ) have sexual encounters with characters after inviting them for coffee. The franchise had over 4,000 news stories published in July 2008, all related to violence, crime and misogyny perpetration. It is hardly surprising that it has been recognized as the most controversial video game franchise in history by Guinness World Records. Of course, millions still love it. But that is another story…
Generating the kind of revenues that make Hollywood envious
GTA games generate the kind of revenue that Hollywood blockbusters can only dream of. GTA 5 hit one billion USD in retail sales within three days, making it the fastest entertainment property overall to hit that milestone at that time. And GTA 6 seems to have followed in its footsteps. While no official figures have been released, it is estimated that nearly 25 million copies of the game were sold on the first day, and its earnings come to around 3.8 billion USD. Just for context, Christopher Nolan’s Odyssey has made USD 1.8 billion at the box office at the time of writing.
It is made in Scotland!
It might be released by a US company (Rockstar Games) and might feature US cities in its gameplay, but Grand Theft Auto is actually made in Edinburgh, Scotland, by Rockstar North, which was previously known as DMA Design, a company that was incorporated in Dublin. So yes, believe it or not, the game that many consider to be classically all-American was actually made by the Brits. And that too, by the ones that wear kilts. Bravehearts, truly.

Honor teams up with cinema camera-maker Arri on the Magic 9 Pro Max
Once again, Honor wants to burnish its Hollywood bona fides.
If there's one thing to expect from the launch of a new Honor phone, it's an attempt to burnish its Hollywood bona fides. The advent of the new Magic 9 Pro Max is a chance for the Chinese giant to, as usual, tell the world about how it's once again redefined mobile cinematography. It's the first proper Honor flagship — and second only to the Robot Phone — to benefit from its partnership with Arri. If you're unfamiliar, the German giant makes the Alexa cinema camera, which has shot at least six films which went on to win an Academy Award for cinematography. If nothing else, if your Instagram reel doesn't at least garner a nomination, you know it's not the hardware's fault.
The Magic 9 Pro Max is the first Honor flagship to use the company's new industrial design first seen on its lower-end N series models. That includes a new camera plateau, albeit with a new color contrast back panel around the frame which puts me in mind of... something. Similarly, this is the first Honor flagship to get the Pro Max moniker, a suffix I don't think I've seen elsewhere in the rest of the mobile industry, but which sounds so cool that you think it might inspire copycats.
Nestled inside, you'll find a Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 system-on-chip with either 12GB or 16GB RAM and the choice of 256GB, 512GB or 1TB storage. Up front, it's packing a 6.8-inch, 2,868 x 1,320 LTPO OLED display with a 1-120Hz refresh rate and 10,000 nits peak brightness. That's paired with an 8,000mAh battery which can support up to 100W wired or 80W wireless charging. Rounding out the useful specs are Wi-Fi 7, space for two SIM cards as well as an eSIM and a 55-megapixel front-facing camera.
Of course, these are all just supporting players for the main event, the Arriflex-inspired triple camera system 'round back. It's equipped with a 200-megapixel, f/1.57 OIS primary lens and a 200-megapixel f/2.6 OIS telephoto, as well as a 50-megapixel f/2.0 ultra-wide camera. Of note is that Honor claims the primary lens has "gimbal" levels of optical stabilization to keep your shots as smooth as possible, no matter how you old it.
To make use of all those megapixels, Honor is launching its first dedicated imaging processor, the H1, and grabbed plenty of Arri's know-how. Honor says the Magic 9 Pro Max uses an end-to-end cinematic workflow, shooting high-end video in Arri LogC3 — the company's version of Log — as well as a series of Arri-created filters and color profiles you can apply to your footage. You'll have a pick of up to 87 Arri looks to apply to your footage, and you can even shoot in Cinema ratios like 2.39:1.
To further bolster its credentials in this arena, Honor is launching a series of accessories in partnership with SmallRig. Equip your phone with the SmallRig camera cage and you'll be able to attach it to either the Honor-branded Teleconverter G200 or the Teleconverter G500. They'll increase the phone's focal length by either 200mm or 500mm, enabling you to shoot distances you'd struggle to capture with AI-enhanced imaging.
Honor's Magic 9 Pro Max is debuting in Malaysia, priced at RM 5,999 (approx $1,455) for the 12GB RAM / 512GB storage option. It'll arrive in the Middle East next month, and take its first bow in the West at some point in January.

Even as Christian communities continue to face attacks allegedly from Hindutva groups across various parts of West Bengal, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) state president Samik Bhattacharya on November 15 issued a warning to Christian missionary school, saying it they were found promoting “anti-India activities”, they would not be allowed to function.
“If any Christian missionary school, due to religious reasons, promotes anti-India activities, we will not let that school run,” he said while addressing a gathering at Birsa Munda’s birth anniversary celebrations in New Alipore, Kolkata.
“Guardians should become alert that an official at a school placed a Pakistani flag on the table of his chamber… in a school here in Kolkata. Please correct yourselves… We will let this happen in West Bengal no matter how powerful they are. All Christian missionaries can take to the streets; we are not opposed to any religion, but sitting in our state, in our country, we will not let you insult saffron [colour]… We will not allow it.”
Prior to issuing the warning, Bhattacharya claimed that a woman BJP worker was prevented from entering a “prestigious school in Kolkata” for wearing a saffron saree. “A prestigious school in Kolkata…I am not naming the school right now because a few days later I will sit outside its gates. One of our sisters, our BJP worker who was seen wearing saffron attire…was told [by the school] that ‘wearing these saris, you cannot come to school, you cannot pronounce the name of lotus flower while teaching the students.’ This is happening in the land of Kolkata where several eminent personalities have walked,” he said.
He further went on to insinuate that Christians were continuing to uphold British mentality in India. “It’s been 75 years since the British left the country, but the mentality has not left. You have come here; you are holding your establishments; you are Catholics, you are Protestants; you can propagate your religion. But remember, this government is not Babur’s government. This government is not trying to uphold British legacies. West Bengal has an independent government,” he said.
A report published by The Telegraph stated that the BJP president alleged that a reputed college in Kolkata was carrying out religious conversions in Asansol forcibly through “allurements”. “There is an obhijato (elite) college in Kolkata whose principal is carrying out religious conversion in Asansol. This cannot be allowed to continue. This is not the government of the Trinamool Congress, this is not the Left Front government…We are against political intervention in any educational institution. We want schools to create their own curriculum,” the report quoted him.
Bhattacharya, however, did not name any Christian missionary schools or colleges or provide any evidence behind the severe allegations he levelled against the community.
Upon being asked about Bhattacharya’s allegations against Christian missionaries, chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on November 17, Tuesday, told the media, “…I get information on this and verify the facts. If the information is true and a written complaint is filed, if an individual did it, action will be taken against the individual; and if it was done institutionally, we will withdraw the NOC given to the institute.”

If the information is true and a written complaint is filed—if an individual did it, action will be taken against the individual; and if it was done institutionally…”

Christian Bodies Condemn Remarks, Issue Statements
The Bangiya Christiya Pariseba (BCP) in a statement on November 18 reacted to Bhattacharya’s statement saying “sweeping accusations without evidence” maligned a peace-loving community and endangered social harmony, and demanded “specific facts, accountability, and immediate legal action”.
BCP posed eight questions to Bhattacharya and the state administration, questioning the lack of legal action against alleged perpetrators of illegal conversion, if any, and the silence over recurring vigilante attacks on Christians. It asked why attacks and vandalism of prayer meetings by ‘militant groups’ had not been condemned, whether such groups were allegedly being used to intimidate Christians, and sought the status of FIRs filed in connection with alleged threats and attacks against the community in the state.

The BCP also demanded documentary evidence of alleged conversions in Christian-run educational institutions, pointing out that millions studied in these schools, and urged ruling party leaders educated in missionary institutions to share their experiences.
The association further questioned the administration’s silence on around 50 alleged attacks on Christian prayer gatherings over the past four to five months, contrasting it with their vocal responses to issues like an official allegedly displaying a Pakistani flag or wearing a saffron saree, without conclusive evidence.
Concerns Ahead of Christmas
Following Bhattacharya’s remarks, Paritosh Canning, moderator of the Church of North India and bishop of the Calcutta diocese, on Sunday sought chief minister Suvendu Adhikari’s intervention against the rising number of attacks against the Christian community in West Bengal. Issuing a statement under the banner of Bengal Christian Council, he urged Adhikari to take appropriate measures to ensure the safety and security of Christians, churches and places of worship, to uphold the constitutionally guaranteed right of practising one’s faith.
“Our concerns are not without reason. Reports of attacks, intimidation and disruption of Christian religious activities have emerged from several districts of Bengal…These reported incidents include attacks on priests, pastors and worshippers, vandalism of churches and crosses, disruption of prayer meetings, intimidation of Christian families and interference with religious activities,” the statement read.
“These developments have caused considerable anxiety and apprehension among members of the Christian community. West Bengal has traditionally been a land of communal harmony…With Christmas approaching, the apprehensions of the Christian community have become particularly serious…the prevailing atmosphere of insecurity has raised genuine concerns about whether Christians will be able to observe their religious services and celebrate Christmas without fear or disruption,” the statement added.
Condemning Bhattacharya’s remarks, representatives of BCP and the West Bengal Association of Christian Schools held a joint press conference on November 16, Monday. Representatives of the associations dismissed the allegations of forceful religious conversion as baseless. They demanded that Bhattacharya name the two institutes and provide evidence to back his claims against Christian missionaries.
